* Vocabulary:
(الْأَعْجَمِينَ): al-Zamakhsharī said: al-aʿjam is one who does not speak clearly and in whose tongue there is ʿujma (non-Arab indistinctness) and istiʿjām; al-aʿjamī is like it, except that the added yāʾ of relation (yāʾ al-nisba) gives an added emphasis. Al-Ḥasan read it as «الأعجميين». Since they could not understand the speech of one who speaks a tongue other than theirs, they called him aʿjam and aʿjamī, likening him to one who does not speak clearly or make himself plain. They also called every creature with a voice among the beasts, birds and others aʿjam. Ḥumayd said:
ولا عربيا شاقه صوت أعجما
(nor an Arab stirred to longing by the voice of a non-speaking creature).
I say: this is the second hemistich of a verse whose first hemistich is:
«ولم أر مثلي شاقه صوت مثلها»
(and I have not seen one like me stirred to longing by the voice of one like her). The verse is from lines by Ḥumayd ibn Thawr, composed when his beloved had departed; among them:
وما هاج هذا الشوق إلا حمامة ... دعت ساق حر ترحة وتندما
(Nothing stirred up this longing but a dove that called her mate in sorrow and regret)
عجبت لها أنّى يكون غناؤها ... فصيحا ولم تفغر بسنطقها فما
(I marvel at her: how can her song be so eloquent when she has not opened a mouth to utter it?) [Translator's note: «بسنطقها» appears to be a misprint for «بمنطقها»/«بنطقها»; the commentary below reads «بنطقها».]
ولم أر مثلي شاقه صوت مثلها ... ولا عربيا شاقه صوت أعجما
(and I have not seen one like me stirred to longing by the voice of one like her, nor an Arab stirred to longing by the voice of a non-speaking creature).
«ساق حر» is a genitive construct compound, and it means the male dove in general. He says: nothing moved this longing and roused it so that it blazed in my heart except a dove that called her mate. «الترحة» is sorrow, the opposite of joy; «التندم» is grieving over what has passed; it is also transmitted as «وترنما», which is beautifying the voice. Both are accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., sorrowing and grieving, or possessed of sorrow and possessed of regret. «أنى» is an interrogative noun meaning "how", and the interrogative here means wonder. «فغر فاه يفغره», of the pattern of «نفع», means he opened it; i.e., while in fact she did not open her mouth to speak, but her voice comes out from her breast. «شاقه» means it caused him longing. «العربي» is the one who speaks clearly, and «الأعجم» is the animal that does not speak clearly; the Arabs transferred it to those whose speech they did not understand and whose meaning they did not grasp, and sometimes they attached the yāʾ of relation to it for intensification of the degree of ʿujma. Between it and «عربي» there is ṭibāq al-taḍādd (antithesis by contrast).
A difficulty has been raised: how can «الأعجم» be given the sound masculine plural, when it is an adjective on the pattern afʿal in the masculine and faʿlāʾ in the feminine, and the condition for pluralizing with yāʾ and nūn or with wāw and nūn is that the adjective not be like that? The answer given is that it is the plural of «أعجمي» with the yāʾ of relation, which was dropped for lightness, like «أشعرين» from «أشعري». The Kufans permit giving the sound masculine plural to an afʿal whose feminine is faʿlāʾ. The author of al-Taḥrīr said: «His words "on some of the aʿjamīn" are the plural of aʿjamī; were it not for this assumption it would not be permissible to give it the sound plural.» The wording of al-Qāmūs is: «al-ʿujm, with ḍamma, and al-ʿajam, with fatḥa on the middle letter, is the opposite of the Arabs; a man and a people are aʿjam. Al-aʿjam is one who does not speak clearly, like al-aʿjamī; also the mute; also Ziyād the poet; also the wave that does not breathe, so it does not spray water and no sound is heard from it. Al-ʿajamī is one whose race is the ʿajam, even if he speaks clearly; its plural is ʿajam.»

* I'rab:
(وَإِنَّهُ لَتَنْزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), brought to establish the truth of those stories and to confirm the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ; for his reporting about the earlier nations, while he is unlettered and neither reads nor writes, can only come by way of revelation. The pronoun refers to the Qur'an, because these stories are part of it. «إن» and its noun (ism), the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «تنزيل رب العالمين» is its khabar (predicate).
(نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ عَلى قَلْبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُنْذِرِينَ): the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «تنزيل». «به» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., accompanied by it, so the bāʾ is of accompaniment (mulābasa). «الروح» is the fāʿil (agent) and «الأمين» an adjective. «على قلبك» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نزل». The lām is of cause (taʿlīl); «تكون» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām, and «من المؤمنين» is the khabar of «تكون». [Translator's note: so in the source; the words of the verse are «من المنذرين».]
(بِلِسانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُبِينٍ): «بلسان» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «المنذرين», because it is a passive participle [Translator's note: so in the source; «المنذرين» is in fact an active participle], i.e., among those who warned in this Arabic tongue, namely Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb, Ismāʿīl and Muhammad, upon them be blessings and peace; or it is a badal (substitute) of «به» with repetition of the governing particle, i.e., he brought it down in a clear Arabic tongue, that is, in the Arabic language.
(وَإِنَّهُ لَفِي زُبُرِ الْأَوَّلِينَ): conjoined to what preceded. «إن» and its noun, the shifted lām, and «في زبر الأولين» is the khabar of «إن»; it means that its mention is recorded in the heavenly scriptures.
(أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةً أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَماءُ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): the hamza is of the interrogative of disapproval, rebuke and reproach; the wāw conjoins to something implied. «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «يكن» is an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive by «لم». «لهم» are attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «آية» and was put before it. «آية» is the fronted khabar of «يكن», and «أن يعلمه» is, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), the noun of «يكن». «علماء بني إسرائيل» is the agent of «يعلمه» [Translator's note: the source prints «بعلمه», evidently a misprint for «يعلمه»]. These scholars are five who gave tidings of the Qur'an: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, Asad, Usayd, Thaʿlaba and Ibn Yāmīn; they embraced Islam and were good in their Islam.
(وَلَوْ نَزَّلْناهُ عَلى بَعْضِ الْأَعْجَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «لو» is conditional, of impossibility (imtināʿiyya). «نزلناه» is a past verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «على بعض الأعجمين» are attached to «نزلناه».
(فَقَرَأَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «قرأه» is a past verb with a latent (mustatir) agent referring to «بعض الأعجمين» and a direct object. «عليهم» are attached to «قرأه». The clause «ما كانوا مؤمنين» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. «به» are attached to «مؤمنين», and «مؤمنين» is the khabar of «كانوا».
(كَذلِكَ سَلَكْناهُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ): the kāf is an adjective of an omitted, fronted maṣdar, i.e., "like this inserting We inserted it into their hearts and settled it there". «سلكناه» is a verb, its agent and its direct object; «في قلوب المجرمين» are attached to «سلكناه».
(لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ): the clause is resumptive, or a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «سلكناه» or of «المجرمين». On the first view, the clause serves as a clarification and summary of what preceded; on the second, the implied sense is "We inserted it while it is not believed in". «لا» is negative; «يؤمنون» is an imperfect verb, nominative, with its agent; «به» are attached to «يؤمنون». «حتى» is a particle of limit and a preposition; «يروا» is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after «حتى»; the wāw is the agent, «العذاب» the direct object and «الأليم» an adjective.
(فَيَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): the fāʾ is a particle of sequence (taʿqīb). Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the meaning of the sequence in His words "and it will come upon them suddenly, and they will say…"? I say: the meaning is not that seeing the punishment, its sudden onset and asking for respite in it follow one another in actual occurrence; the meaning is rather their ordering in severity. It is as if it were said: they will not believe in the Qur'an until their seeing the punishment comes about; then what is more severe than that, namely its overtaking them suddenly; then what is more severe than that, namely their asking for respite while it is certain that it will be refused. An example of this is that you say to one you are admonishing: "If you do evil, the righteous will detest you, and then Allah will detest you." By this ordering you do not intend that Allah's detestation comes after the detestation of the righteous; your intent is only to rank the gravity of the matter for the evildoer.» Thus al-Zamakhsharī sounded the depths of the Noble Qur'an and comprehended its hidden matters with the comprehension of an expert in the places of its secrets. «يأتيهم» is conjoined to «يروا»; the agent is latent, its implied form being "huwa" (it), and the hāʾ is the direct object. «بغتة» is a ḥāl. The wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause «لا يشعرون» its khabar.
(فَيَقُولُوا هَلْ نَحْنُ مُنْظَرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, as above, and the whole speech is placed early though meant to be later [Translator's note: literally "fronted from a postponement"]. «يقولوا» is conjoined to «يأتيهم». «هل» is an interrogative particle, «نحن» a mubtadaʾ and «منظرون» its khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The meaning of the interrogative here is regret and the deeming unlikely of what is impossible, namely their being granted respite after the punishment has befallen them.

* Benefits:
The conditions of the sound masculine plural:
Everything, noun or adjective, that is given the sound masculine plural is subject to three conditions:
a- Being free of the feminine tāʾ; so this plural is not formed from nouns such as «طلحة», nor from adjectives such as «علّامة» (with doubled lām), lest the markers of feminine and masculine be combined in them.
b- Being for a masculine; so this plural is not formed from a feminine proper name such as «زينب», nor from an adjective of the feminine such as «حائض».
c- Being for a rational being, because this plural is specific to rational beings; so one does not pluralize thus, for example, «واشق» as the name of a dog or «سابق» as an adjective of a horse.
Then it is required that it be either a proper name that is not compounded by blending (tarkīb mazjī) nor by predication (tarkīb isnādī); so a blended compound such as «معدي كرب» and «سيبويه» is not pluralized thus. It has been said that what ends in «ويه» is given this plural, so one says «سيبويهون», and some drop «ويه» [Translator's note: the source prints «وبه»] and say «سيبون». As for the genitive-construct compound, the first of the two terms is pluralized and annexed to the second, so one says «غلامو زيد» and «غلامي زيد»; the Kufans pluralize both together. Or an adjective that accepts the tāʾ intended for the meaning of femininity — so this plural is not formed from, e.g., «علامة» and «نسابة», because the tāʾ in them is for emphasizing intensiveness, not intended for the meaning of femininity; or an adjective that does not accept the tāʾ but indicates preference (tafḍīl). The adjective that does not accept the tāʾ is like «قائم» and «مذنب»: you say «قائمة» and «مذنبة»; [Translator's note: so in the source; the examples «قائم» and «مذنب» in fact accept the tāʾ, as the following words show, so the intended sense is evidently "the adjective that accepts the tāʾ".] and the adjective that indicates preference is like «أفضل». These three kinds of adjectives are given this plural just as they are pluralized with alif and tāʾ, so one says «قائمون», «مذنبون» and «أفضلون» just as one says «قائمات», «مذنبات» and «فضليات». So this plural is not formed from, e.g., «جريح» in the sense of «مجروح», «صبور» in the sense of «صابر», «سكران», «أحمر» and «أعجم», for they do not accept the tāʾ and do not indicate preference: because «جريح» and «صبور» are among the words in which masculine and feminine are alike; the feminine of «سكران» is «سكرى», the feminine of «أحمر» is «حمراء» and the feminine of «أعجم» is «عجماء». So one does not say «جريحون», «صبورون», «سكرانون» and «أحمرون», just as one does not say «جريحات», «صبورات», «سكرانات», «حمراوات» and «عجماوات». If they were made proper names, both plurals would be permissible.

dervis-irab:204-220.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَبِعَذابِنا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ): the hamza is of the interrogative of rebuke, mockery and disapproval, and the fāʾ conjoins to something implied that the context requires, whose determination has preceded. The implied sense is: "Will their state be as was mentioned — asking for respite when the painful punishment descends — and yet they seek to hasten it?" Thus did some grammarians determine it, but it is not free of ambiguity; it is better to determine it as: "Are they heedless of that, despite its being certain and established, and so they seek to hasten it?" The preposition and its genitive noun were put first for two reasons: a verbal one, namely observing the verse-endings (fawāṣil), and a semantic one, namely signalling that the focus of the disapproval and rebuke is that the thing they seek to hasten is the punishment. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يستعجلون».
(أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ مَتَّعْناهُمْ سِنِينَ): the hamza is interrogative, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «رأيت» is conjoined to «فيقولوا», what lies between them being parenthetical. The tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent) of «رأيت». «رأيت» means "inform me", so it takes two objects, the first a single word and the other, usually, an interrogative clause. «إن» is conditional; «متعناهم» is a past verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «سنين» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to «متعناهم».
(ثُمَّ جاءَهُمْ ما كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ): «ثم» is a conjunction; «جاءهم» is a verb and its direct object; «ما» is the agent of «جاءهم»; the clause «كانوا» is the ṣila (relative clause); the wāw is the noun of «كان» and the clause «يوعدون» its khabar (predicate).
Further: «أفرأيت» and «جاءهم» contend (tanāzuʿ) for His words «ما كانوا يوعدون». If you give government to the second, namely «جاءهم», as given in the i'rab above, you make «ما كانوا» nominative by it as its agent; the first object of «أرأيت» is its pronoun, but it was omitted, and the second object is the interrogative clause in His words «ما أغنى عنهم». There must be a linking element between this clause and the omitted first object, and it is implied, its implied form being: "Have you considered what they were promised?" If you give government to the first, you make «ما كانوا» accusative by it as its direct object and imply in «جاءهم» an agent for it; the interrogative clause is likewise a second object, and the returning pronoun is implied as established in the previous view. The condition is parenthetical and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted. The discussion of this expression was given in full in Sūrat al-Anʿām. All this only works on our view that «ما» is interrogative, and their explaining it as negation does not harm us, for the interrogative may come with the sense of negation. But if you make it negative, it becomes a particle, and that does not work, because the second object of «أرأيت» can only be an interrogative clause. This was mentioned in detail, along with the views of the grammarians, in Sūrat al-Anʿām, so refresh your acquaintance with it.
(ما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يُمَتَّعُونَ): «ما» is interrogative, as stated, a fronted direct object of «أغنى». «أغنى» is a past verb and «عنهم» are attached to «أغنى». «ما» is maṣdariyya or a relative; either way it together with what it governs, or it alone, is the agent of «أغنى». The implied sense is "what did their enjoyment avail them", or "what they were given to enjoy of the enjoyment of the worldly life". The interrogative is one of disapproval meaning negation. It has been said that «ما» is negative, and there is no difference between the two, as stated.
(وَما أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا لَها مُنْذِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; «ما» is negative; «أهلكنا» is a verb and its agent; «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and «قرية» is genitive (majrūr) by «من» in form and accusative in position as the object of «أهلكنا». «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «لها» is a fronted khabar and «منذرون» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «قرية» or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it, which is made permissible by the preceding negation. Al-Zamakhsharī has given a fine view on an expression like this before [Translator's note: the source's wording «وقد تقدم الزمخشري رأي» appears to be a misprint for «وقد تقدم للزمخشري رأي»], and we repeat it here. He said: «If you say: how was the wāw dropped from the clause after «إلا», whereas it was not dropped from it in His words "And We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree"? I say: the basic rule is to drop the wāw, because the clause is an adjective of «قرية»; when it is added, it is to emphasize the joining of the adjective to the thing described, as in His words "seven, and the eighth of them their dog".»
(ذِكْرى وَما كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ): «ذكرى» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), in the sense that they warn for the sake of admonition and reminder. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "this is a reminder", the clause being parenthetical. Al-Kisāʾī parsed it as a ḥāl, i.e., "reminding". Al-Zajjāj parsed it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the governing word being «منذرون», because it carries the sense of "reminding with a reminder", i.e., "this is a reminder", the clause being parenthetical; and al-Kisāʾī parsed it as a ḥāl, i.e., "reminding". [Translator's note: so in the source; the last part of this paragraph repeats the preceding sentences, apparently through a printing error.]
(وَما تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّياطِينُ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «تنزلت» is a past verb; «به» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «تنزلت», and the pronoun refers to the Qur'an; «الشياطين» is the agent of «تنزلت».
(وَما يَنْبَغِي لَهُمْ وَما يَسْتَطِيعُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, «ما» is negative, and «ينبغي» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), referring to the Qur'an; «لهم» are attached to «ينبغي». «وما يستطيعون» is conjoined to «ما ينبغي», and the object of «يستطيعون» is omitted, its implied form being "that".
(إِنَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّمْعِ لَمَعْزُولُونَ): the clause gives the reason for their inability to bring it down. «إن» and its noun; «عن السمع» are attached to «معزولون»; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and «معزولون» is the khabar of «إن».
(فَلا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُعَذَّبِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (of the implied condition); the address is to the Prophet ﷺ while someone else is intended. «لا» is the prohibitive lā; «تدع» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لا», its agent latent, its implied form being "anta" (you). «مع» is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «إلها» and was put before it. «إلها» is the direct object and «آخر» an adjective of «إلها». «فتكون»: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (sababiyya), and «تكون» is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ; the noun of «تكون» is latent, its implied form being "anta", and «من المعذبين» is the khabar of «تكون».
(وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «أنذر» is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "anta"; «عشيرتك» is the direct object and «الأقربين» an adjective. A full discussion of this warning will come in the Benefits section.
(وَاخْفِضْ جَناحَكَ لِمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): also conjoined. «اخفض جناحك» is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; «لمن» are attached to «اخفض»; the clause «اتبعك» is the ṣila of «من», and «من المؤمنين» is a ḥāl.
(فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ فَقُلْ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «عصوك» is a past verb, its agent and its direct object, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). «فقل»: the fāʾ links the apodosis. «إن» and its noun, and «بريء» its khabar; «مما» are attached to «بريء»; the clause «تعملون» is the ṣila; and the clause «إني بريء» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), which is why the hamza of «إن» is given kasra.
(وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ): conjoined to what preceded; «على العزيز» are attached to «توكل».
(الَّذِي يَراكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ): «الذي» is an adjective of «العزيز الرحيم»; the clause «يراك» is the ṣila; «حين» is an adverb attached to «يراك»; the clause «تقوم» is genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and what «تقوم» attaches to is omitted, i.e., "to the prayer".
(وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِي السَّاجِدِينَ): conjoined to the kāf in «يراك»; «في الساجدين» is a ḥāl, «في» meaning "with", i.e., praying with the congregation. It is reported from Muqātil that he asked Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah be pleased with him: "Do you find prayer in congregation in the Qur'an?" and he recited this verse. Some said that what is meant by «الساجدين» is the believers, i.e., He sees you passing through the loins and wombs of the believers from the time of Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ down to ʿAbd Allāh and Āmina.
(إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): «إن» and its noun; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; «السميع العليم» are two khabars of «إن» or of the pronoun, and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن».

* Benefits:
Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger ﷺ to warn the nearest and then the next nearest. When Allah the Exalted sent down «وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين», he invited them to the house of his uncle Abū Ṭālib; they were at that time forty men, one more or one less, among them his uncles. He warned them, saying: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, if I told you that at the foot of this mountain there are horsemen, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you ahead of a severe punishment." It is also related that he said: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, O sons of Hāshim, O sons of ʿAbd Manāf, ransom yourselves from the Fire, for I can avail you nothing." Then he said: "O ʿĀʾisha daughter of Abū Bakr, O Ḥafṣa daughter of ʿUmar, O Fāṭima daughter of Muhammad, O Ṣafiyya aunt of Muhammad, buy yourselves from the Fire, for I can avail you nothing."
There are other reports that do not depart from this meaning; we content ourselves with what has been given of them.

dervis-irab:221-227.t:
* I'rab:
(هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ عَلى مَنْ تَنَزَّلُ الشَّياطِينُ): resumptive speech, brought to refute his being a soothsayer (kāhin) who receives from the devils. «هل» is an interrogative particle; «أنبئكم» is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «على من» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تنزل»; it was put first to give it importance and because the interrogative has the front of the sentence. It suspends (taʿlīq) the verb of informing from governing, and the clause stands in place of the second and third objects. «تنزل» is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped, the original being «تتنزل»; «الشياطين» is the agent of «تنزل».
(تَنَزَّلُ عَلى كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تنزل», and it is a badal (substitute) of the preposition and genitive noun before it. «أفاك» is the muḍāf ilayhi of «كل», and «أثيم» an adjective. They are the soothsayers and false claimants to prophecy, such as Shiqq, Saṭīḥ, Musaylima and Ṭalḥa [Translator's note: presumably Ṭulayḥa al-Asadī is meant].
(يُلْقُونَ السَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كاذِبُونَ): «يلقون» is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent. It refers to the devils, in which case the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it refers to «كل أفاك أثيم», inasmuch as that is plural in meaning, in which case the clause is resumptive or an adjective of «كل أفاك أثيم». The meaning of their "casting the hearing" is their listening intently to the Highest Assembly so as to steal something [Translator's note: the source prints «ليسترقو»], or casting the thing heard to the soothsayers. «السمع» is the direct object. The wāw is of ḥāl; «أكثرهم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «كاذبون» its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl.
(وَالشُّعَراءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغاوُونَ): also resumptive speech, brought to refute his being a poet, as they claimed. An ample discussion of poetry, and of who the poets are whom the deviators follow, will come in the Benefits section. «الشعراء» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يتبعهم» its khabar; «يتبعهم» is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object, and «الغاوون» is the postponed agent.
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وادٍ يَهِيمُونَ): the clause is explicative (mufassira). The hamza is of the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you). «أن» and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of «تر». «في كل واد» are attached to «يهيمون»; «يهيمون» is an imperfect verb and its agent, and the clause is the khabar of «أنهم». It is also permissible to attach the preposition and its genitive noun to an omitted word which is the khabar, the clause «يهيمون» being a ḥāl. The representation of their going into every path of speech by the image of a valley will be discussed in the Rhetoric section.
(وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ ما لا يَفْعَلُونَ): a conjoined clause.
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً): «إلا» is a particle of exception, and «الذين» is excepted (mustathnā) from the censured poets. The clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause); «عملوا الصالحات» is conjoined to «آمنوا» and falls within the scope of the ṣila; «ذكروا الله» is also conjoined; «كثيرا» is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e., "they remembered Allah with much remembrance", or an adjective of an omitted adverb of time, i.e., "much time".
(وَانْتَصَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا): conjoined to what preceded. «ما» is maṣdariyya, i.e., "after their being wronged", an instance of annexing the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object.
(وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, the sīn is a particle of futurity, «يعلم» is an imperfect verb and «الذين» its agent; the clause «ظلموا» is the ṣila. «أي منقلب» is accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, because «أي» is parsed according to what it is annexed to; it has suspended «يعلم» from governing. Note that what governs «أي» is «ينقلبون», not «يعلم», because interrogative nouns are not governed by what precedes them. Al-Naḥḥās said: «The truth of the matter is that the interrogative is one meaning and what precedes it is another meaning; if it governed it, some meanings would enter into others.»

* Rhetoric:
In the words of the Exalted «ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون» there is a subtle istiʿāra tamthīliyya (representational metaphor): there is no valley, no ravines and no wandering; it is only penetration into the regions of speech, going astray in descriptions, amatory verse (taghazzul), tashbīb and nasīb, and little concern for the honour they violate and the rumours they spread. The details of that will come in the discussion of poetry in the Benefits section. It is related of al-Farazdaq that Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik heard his words:
فبتن بجانبي مصرعات ... وبت أفض إغلاق الختام
(They spent the night beside me, laid low, while I spent it breaking the locks of the seals.)
and said: "The prescribed punishment (ḥadd) is now due upon you." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah has averted the ḥadd from me by His words «وأنهم يقولون ما لا يفعلون»."

* Benefits:
1- The merit of poetry:
The exception of the righteous poets — those who defend their homelands, call to virtues and reform, and depict the faults and evils of society in order to mend its cracks — shows the lofty rank and high station poetry has. Al-Bukhārī related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Some poetry is wisdom." From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and began speaking in a certain way, and he said: 'Some eloquence is magic, and some poetry is wisdom.'" Abū Dāwūd transmitted it. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Poetry is speech; some of it is good and some of it is ugly, so take the good and leave the ugly." Al-Shaʿbī said: "Abū Bakr used to compose poetry, ʿUmar used to compose poetry, ʿUthmān used to compose poetry, and ʿAlī was a better poet than the three, may Allah be pleased with them all."
Between verse and prose:
The author of al-ʿUmda said: «The speech of the Arabs is of two kinds: versified and prose, and each of them has three grades: excellent, middling and poor. When the two grades agree in measure and are equal in value, and neither has any superiority over the other, the judgment goes to poetry, as is evident in the naming, because every versified piece is better than every prose piece of its kind by customary acknowledgement. Do you not see that pearls — which are the brother of speech and its kin, to which it is compared and by which it is likened — when they are scattered (manthūr), are not safe and are not used for the purpose for which they were acquired and selected, even though they are of higher worth and greater price; but when they are strung (manẓūm), that preserves them better from being cheapened and shows their beauty better despite much use. Likewise speech, when it is scattered, is dispersed in the ears and rolls away from natural dispositions.»
Lying is blameworthy except from poets:
Among its merits is that lying, whose ugliness people agree upon, is good in it; and it suffices you that it made lying good and forgave its ugliness. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ threatened Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr when he had written to his brother Bujayr forbidding him from Islam and had mentioned the Prophet ﷺ in a way that angered him. His brother sent to him: "Woe to you! The Prophet has threatened you because of what reached him about you; he had threatened men in Mecca among those who satirized him and harmed him, and he killed them — meaning Ibn Khaṭal and Ibn Ḥubāba — and those who remain of the poets of Quraysh, such as Ibn al-Zibaʿrā and Hubayra ibn Abī Wahb, have fled in every direction. If you have any need for your life, fly to the Messenger of Allah, for he does not kill one who comes repenting; otherwise flee to your place of safety, for by Allah he will kill you." The earth became narrow for him, and he came to the Messenger of Allah in disguise. When the Prophet [Translator's note: the source prints «البني», a misprint for «النبي»] had prayed the dawn prayer, Kaʿb put his hand in the hand of the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr has come seeking safe-conduct [Translator's note: the source prints «مسنأمنا», a misprint for «مستأمنا»], repenting; will you grant him safety, so that I bring him to you?" He said: "He is safe." Then Kaʿb uncovered his face and said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah; this is the place of one who seeks refuge with you. I am Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr." The Messenger of Allah granted him safety, and Kaʿb recited his ode whose beginning is:
بانت سعاد فقلبي اليوم متبول ... متيّم إثرها لم يفد مكبول
(Suʿād has departed, and my heart today is love-sick, enslaved in her wake, a captive unransomed.)
In it, after his amatory prelude and the mention of the intensity of his fear and dread, he says:
أنبئت أن رسول الله أوعدني ... والعفو عند رسول الله مأمول
(I was told that the Messenger of Allah threatened me, and pardon is hoped for from the Messenger of Allah.)
مهلا هداك الذي أعطاك نافلة الق ... سر آن فيها مواعيظ وتفصيل
(Gently! May He guide you who gave you the gift of the Qur'an, in which are admonitions and detailed exposition.) [Translator's note: «الق ... سر آن» is as printed in the source; the word is «القرآن», split across the hemistichs.]
لا تأخذنّي بأقوال الوشاة فلم ... أذنب وقد كثرت فيّ الأقاويل
(Do not seize me on the words of slanderers, for I have not sinned, though the rumours about me have multiplied.)
The Prophet did not reproach him for his words — and he would not have threatened him over a falsehood — rather he pardoned him and gave him his cloak (burda). Muʿāwiya bought it from him for thirty thousand dirhams — al-ʿUtbī said for twenty thousand — and it is the one the caliphs inherited, wearing it on Fridays and festivals.
It is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by Ḥassān while he was reciting poetry in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "A grumbling like the grumbling of a camel?" Ḥassān said: "Leave me alone, ʿUmar; by Allah, you know that I used to recite in this mosque before one who was better than you, and he did not object to it." ʿUmar said: "You have spoken the truth."
The author of al-ʿUmda said: «As for the argument of one who does not understand the drift of the speech from the words of the Exalted «والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون، ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون، وأنهم يقولون ما لا يفعلون», it is an error and a bad interpretation, because what is meant by this text is the poets of the polytheists who attacked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with satire and touched him with harm. As for the believers other than them, they are not included in any of that. Do you not hear how Allah the Mighty and Majestic excepted them and drew attention to them, saying: «إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وذكروا الله كثيرا وانتصروا من بعد ما ظلموا»? He means the Prophet's poets who defended him and answered the polytheists on his behalf, such as Ḥassān ibn Thābit, Kaʿb ibn Mālik and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa. The Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the source prints «صلى الله عليهم وسلم»] said of them: "These few are harder on Quraysh than the shower of arrows" [Translator's note: the source prints «نصح النبل»; the familiar wording is «نضح النبل»], and he said to Ḥassān ibn Thābit: "Satirize them — meaning Quraysh — and the Holy Spirit is with you; by Allah, your satire is harder on them than the fall of arrows in the darkness before dawn. And meet Abū Bakr, so that he teaches you those foibles [of theirs]." If poetry were forbidden or disliked, the Prophet would not have taken poets whom he rewarded for poetry, ordered to compose it and listened to it from them.
As for his words ﷺ: "That the belly of one of you be filled with pus until it corrupts it is better for him than that it be filled with poetry," this refers only to one in whose heart poetry has prevailed [Translator's note: the source prints «من غلب الشعراء على قلبه», "whose heart the poets prevailed over"; «الشعر» seems intended] and taken possession of him, until it distracts him from his religion and the performance of his obligations and prevents him from the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.»
Many of the rightly guided caliphs, the eminent Companions and Successors, and the famous jurists composed poetry.
Of that is the poetry of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him. They said: his name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, and it is said that ʿAtīq was a nickname of his. He said, concerning the raid of ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith [Translator's note: the poem's lines are broken across lines in the source; they are given here as whole verses, with the text unchanged]:
أمن طيف سلمى بالبطاح الدمائث ... أرقت أوامر في العشيرة حادث
(Was it from the phantom of Salmā in the soft valleys that I lay sleepless, or from something that has befallen the clan?)
ترى من لؤي فرقة لا يصدّها ... عن الكفر تذكير ولا بعث باعث
(You see a band of Luʾayy whom neither reminder nor any rousing turns back from disbelief.)
رسول أتاهم صادق فتكذّبوا ... عليه وقالوا: لست فينا بماكث
(A truthful Messenger came to them, and they belied him and said: "You shall not remain among us.")
إذا ما دعوناهم إلى الحق أدبروا ... وهرّوا هرير المجمرات اللواهث
(Whenever we called them to the truth they turned away and snarled like panting dogs.)
فكم قد متتنا فيهم بقرابة ... وترك التقى شيء لهم غير كارث
(How often we appealed to them by kinship! Yet abandoning piety is something that does not trouble them.)
فإن يرجعوا عن كفرهم وعقوقهم ... فما طيبات الحلّ مثل الخبائث
(If they turn back from their disbelief and undutifulness — the good lawful things are not like the foul ones.)
وإن يركبوا طغيانهم وضلالهم ... فليس عذاب الله عنهم بلابث
(And if they ride on in their transgression and error, Allah's punishment will not be slow to reach them.)
فأولى برب الراقصات عشية ... حراجيح تخدي في السريح الرثائث
(I swear by the Lord of the camels that trot at evening, lean ones pacing in worn-out sandals,)
كأدم ظباء حول مكة عكف ... يردن حياض البئر ذات النبائث
(like tawny gazelles staying about Mecca, coming down to the troughs of the well with its dug-up earth,)
لئن لم يفيقوا عاجلا من ضلالهم ... ولست إذا آليت قولا بحانث
(that if they do not soon wake from their error — and when I swear an oath I do not break it —)
لتبتدرنهم غارة ذات مصدق ... تحرم أطهار النساء الطوامث
(a raid of true valour will surely rush upon them, forbidding [to them] the pure and the menstruating women alike,)
تغادر قتلى تعصب الطير حولهم ... ولا يرأف الكفار رأف ابن حارث
(leaving slain men about whom the birds flock; and Ibn Ḥārith shows the disbelievers no pity.)
فأبلغ بني سهم لديك رسالة ... وكل كفور يبتغي الشر باحث
(So convey from me a message to Banū Sahm and to every ungrateful one who seeks out evil:)
فإن شتموا عرضي على سوء رأيهم ... فإني من أعراضهم غير شاعث
(if in their ill judgment they revile my honour, I shall not stain theirs.)
Here it must be pointed out that Ibn Hishām said in his Sīra: «Most of the people of knowledge deny that this ode is by Abū Bakr.»
Of the poetry of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him — who was among the most discerning critics of poetry in his time and the most penetrating in his knowledge of it:
هوّن عليك فإن الأمو ... ر بكف الإله مقاديرها
(Take it easy, for the measures of all affairs are in the hand of God;)
فليس يأتيك منهيها ... ولا قاصر عنك مأمورها
(what is forbidden of them will not come to you, nor will what is decreed fall short of you.)
Also of his poetry, when he had put on a new cloak and people looked at him:
لا شيء مما ترى تبقى بشاشته ... يبقى الإله ويفنى المال والولد
(Nothing you see keeps its brightness; God remains, while wealth and children perish.)
لم تغن عن هرمز يوما خزائنه ... والخلد قد حاولت عاد فما خلدوا
(His treasures did not avail Hurmuz one day; ʿĀd sought immortality, yet they did not endure.)
ولا سليمان إذ تجري الرياح له ... والجنّ والإنس فيما بينها ترد
(Nor Solomon, when the winds ran for him, and jinn and men came and went between them.)
حوض هنالك مورود بلا كذب ... لا بد من ورده يوما كما وردوا
(There is a watering-place there, truly to be reached; one day it must be reached, as they reached it.)
Of the poetry of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him:
غنى النفس يغني النفس حتى يكفّها ... وإن عضّها حتى يضر بها الفقر
(Richness of soul enriches the soul until it restrains it, even if poverty bites it until it harms it.)
وما عمرة- فاصبر لها إن لقيتها- بكائنة إلا سيتبعها يسر
(No hardship — so be patient with it if you meet it — comes to be but ease will follow it.) [Translator's note: the source prints «عمرة»; the sense requires «عسرة» (hardship).]
Of the poetry of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, what he said on the day of Ṣiffīn, mentioning Hamdān and their support of him:
ولما رأيت الخيل ترجم بالقنا ... نواصيّها حمر النحور دوامي
(When I saw the horses pelted with spears in their forelocks, their breasts red and bleeding,)
وأعرض نقع في السماء كأنه ... عجاجة دجن ملبس بقتام
(and dust spread broad in the sky like the cloud of a gloomy day clothed in murk,)
ونادى ابن هند في الكلاع وحمير ... وكندة في لخم وحيّ جذام
(and the son of Hind called out among al-Kalāʿ and Ḥimyar, Kinda, Lakhm and the tribe of Judhām,)
تيمّمت همدان الذين هم هم ... - إذا ناب دهر- جنتي وسهامي
(I made for Hamdān, who are — when fate strikes — my shield and my arrows.)
فجاوبني من خيل همدان عصبة ... فوارس من همدان غير لئام
(A band of Hamdān's horsemen answered me, knights of Hamdān, no base men.)
فخاضوا لظاها واستطاروا شرارها ... وكانوا لدى الهيجا كشرب مدام
(They plunged into its blaze and scattered its sparks, and in the fray they were like drinkers of wine.)
فلو كنت بوّابا على باب جنة ... لقلت لهمدان ادخلوا بسلام
(Were I a gatekeeper at the gate of Paradise, I would say to Hamdān: "Enter in peace.")
Of the poetry of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, when he came out to his companions dyed (with henna), related by al-Mubarrad:
تسوّد أعلاها وتأبى أصولها ... فليت الذي يسودّ منها هو الأصل
(Its tips turn black, but its roots refuse; would that what turns black were the root.)
Of the poetry of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, when his brother al-Ḥasan reproached him concerning his wife:
لعمرك انني لأحب دارا ... تحل بها سكينته والرباب
(By your life, I love a house in which Sukayna and al-Rabāb dwell;)
أحبهما وأبذل جلّ مالي ... وليس للائمي عندي عتاب
(I love them both and spend most of my wealth, and the one who blames me has no reproach from me.)
Many of the caliphs composed poetry. Of the poetry of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz:
أيقظان أنت اليوم أم أنت حالم ... وكيف يطيق النوم حيران هائم
(Are you awake today or dreaming? And how can one bewildered and distraught bear to sleep?)
فلو كنت يقظان الغداة لحرقت ... جفونا لعينيك الدموع السواجم
(Were you awake this morning, pouring tears would have burnt the lids of your eyes.)
نهارك يا مغرور سهو وغفلة ... وليلك نوم والردى لك لازم
(Your day, O deluded one, is distraction and heedlessness, your night is sleep, and death clings to you.)
وتشغل فيما سوف تكره غبّه ... كذلك في الدنيا تعيش البهائم
(You busy yourself with what you will hate the outcome of; thus do beasts live in this world.)
Among the jurists, Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī was famous for poetry; he was among the most versatile of people in poetry, and he is the one who said:
ومتعب العيس مرتاحا إلى بلد ... والموت يطلبه في ذلك البلد
(Many a one wears out his camels, eager for a land, while death seeks him in that very land;)
وضاحك والمنايا فوق مفرقه ... لو كان يعلم غيبا مات من كمد
(and many a one laughs while death hovers over his head; if he knew the unseen he would die of grief.)
من كان لم يؤت علما في بقاء غد ... ماذا تفكره في رزق بعد غد
(One who has been given no knowledge that he will survive tomorrow — why does he think about provision for the day after?)
Among his famous masterpieces are his words on fortune:
الجدّ يدني كلّ شيء شاسع ... والجدّ يفتح كل باب مغلق
(Fortune brings near every distant thing, and fortune opens every closed door.)
فإذا سمعت بأن مجدورا حوى ... عودا فأورق في يديه فصدق
(If you hear that a fortunate man took hold of a dry stick and it put forth leaves in his hands, believe it.) [Translator's note: the source prints «مجدورا»; the sense requires «مجدودا» (fortunate).]
وإذا سمعت بأن محروما أتى ... ماء ليشربه فجفّ فحقق
(And if you hear that an unfortunate man came to water to drink it and it dried up, take it as true.)
وأحقّ خلق الله بالهم امرؤ ... ذو همة يبلى برزق ضيق
(The most deserving of God's creatures of worry is a man of high aspiration afflicted with narrow means.)
ولربّما عرضت لنفسي فكرة ... فأودّ منها أنني لم أخلق
(And sometimes a thought presents itself to me, so that because of it I wish I had not been created.)
[Translator's note: in the source the lines of this poem and of the preceding ones are broken across lines; they are given here as whole verses with the text unchanged.]
What we have cited as evidence suffices us, for more may take us away from our purpose.
Boileau's advice to the poet:
We close the discussion with the valuable advice that the French writer Boileau gave to the poet, which in summary is: the poet must keep himself clear of licentiousness; it is true that depicting love is permitted, but only so long as there is no kind of vulgarity in the depiction. He should strip himself of envy, for it is one of the banes of men of letters, a vice which, if found in one of them, indicates the weakness of his gifts.
Then he should be good company and pleasant in conversation. Further, among the things that disgrace a poet is directing his concern to earning money; on the contrary, it befits him to strive to attain glory. He must not lower the standing of poetry, that divine art which in times past refined souls, kindled patriotism in them and taught wisdom and virtue.
2- Who was Saṭīḥ the soothsayer:
History relates that Saṭīḥ [Translator's note: the source prints «سطحيا»] al-Ghassānī was the greatest soothsayer among people. He warned of the Flood of al-ʿArim. His body could be folded as a garment is folded, except for the skull of his head, and if it was touched with the hand it left an impression on it because of the softness of its bone. He always lay stretched flat on the ground. He lived 150 years, as it is said, and died on the night Muhammad ﷺ was born. Among his soothsaying is this: on the night the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was born, the hall (īwān) of Kisrā shook and fourteen of its battlements fell, and the people of the kingdom took that as a grave matter. The governor of Syria wrote to Kisrā that the valley of al-Samāwa had been cut off that night; the governor of Yemen wrote to him that the lake of Sāwa had sunk that night; the governor of Tiberias wrote to him that the water had not flowed that night in the lake of Tiberias; and the governor of Persia wrote to him that the fire had gone out that night. When the letters came to him one after another, he displayed his throne and came out to the people of his kingdom and told them the news. The Mōbadhān (chief priest) said: "O King, I saw a vision that night that terrified me: I saw unruly camels leading Arab horses until they plunged into the Tigris and spread through our lands." He said: "What do you have regarding its interpretation?" He said: "I have nothing, but send to your governor in al-Ḥīra to dispatch to you a man of their scholars, for they are people with knowledge of events." So he sent him ʿAbd al-Masīḥ ibn Nufayla al-Ghassānī, and Kisrā told him the news. He said: "O King, I have nothing about it, but equip me to go to my maternal uncle Saṭīḥ." So he equipped him, and when he came to him he found him at the point of death. He called to him, but he did not answer, so he said:
أصمّ أم يسمع غطريف اليمن ... أتاك شيخ الحيّ من آل سنن
أبيض فضفاض الرداء والرسن
(Is the chief of Yemen deaf, or does he hear? The elder of the tribe of the house of Sanan has come to you, fair, with ample cloak and halter.)
Saṭīḥ raised his head to him and said [in rhymed prose]: "ʿAbd al-Masīḥ, on a swift camel, has come to Saṭīḥ, when he is at the edge of the grave. The king of the Banū Sāsān sent you, because of the shaking of the hall, the dying out of the fires, and the vision of the Mōbadhān: he saw unruly camels leading Arab horses until they plunged into the river and spread through the lands. O ʿAbd al-Masīḥ, when the recitation appears, the valley of al-Samāwa overflows, and the bearer of the staff appears, then Syria will not be Syria for Saṭīḥ. Of them there will reign kings and queens to the number of the battlements that fell, and all that is coming will come." Then he said:
إن كان ملك بني ساسان أفرطهم ... فإن ذا الدهر أطوار دهارير
(If the kingdom of the Banū Sāsān has passed them by, this fortune is phases of vicissitudes.)
منهم بنو الصرح بهرام وأخوته ... والهرمزان وسابور وسابور
(Among them were the lords of the palace, Bahrām and his brothers, al-Hurmuzān, Sābūr and Sābūr.)
فربما أصبحوا منهم بمنزلة ... يهاب صولهم الأسد المهاصير
(Often they stood in such a rank that the fierce lions feared their assault.)
حثوا المطي وجدوا في رحيلهم ... فما يقوم لهم سرج ولا كور
(They urged on their mounts and hurried in their departure, and neither saddle nor camel-saddle could hold them.)
والناس أبناء علات فمن علموا ... أن قد أقل فمحقور ومهجور
(People are sons of one father by different mothers: whomever they know to have become poor is despised and shunned.)
والخير والشر مقرونان في قرن ... والخير متبع والشر محذور
(Good and evil are tied together in one rope; good is followed and evil is guarded against.)
He went to Kisrā and told him, and that grieved him; he said: "Until fourteen kings of us reign, time will have turned." All of them reigned within forty years.

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* I'rab:
(قالَ: أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينا وَلِيداً وَلَبِثْتَ فِينا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ) An omitted element must necessarily be implied here, namely: "So the two of them set off for Pharaoh's gate, and were not given leave to enter for a year, until the gatekeeper said: 'There is a man here who claims to be the messenger of the Lord of the worlds.' Pharaoh said: 'Let him in, perhaps we shall laugh at him.' So the two delivered the message to him, and he recognised Moses, because he had been raised in his house, and said to him: ألم نربك (Did we not raise you...)". The hamza is for affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; نربك is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; the kāf is the direct object; فينا is attached to نربك; وليدا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ولبثت is a verb and agent; فينا is attached to لبثت; ومن عمرك is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of سنين; and سنين is an adverbial attached also to لبثت.
(وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; فعلت is a verb and agent; فعلتك is a direct object or an absolute object; التي is an adjective; the clause فعلت is its ṣila (relative clause); the wāw is a ḥāl-wāw; أنت is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and من الكافرين its khabar (predicate), that is, those who deny my favour. The deed that Moses had done was the killing of his baker, the Copt. (قالَ فَعَلْتُها إِذاً وَأَنَا مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ) قال is a past verb, that is, Moses; فعلتها is a verb, agent and direct object, or an absolute object, that is, "I did the deed"; إذن is a particle of requital, standing in the place of the answer; the wāw is the ḥāl-wāw; أنا is the mubtadaʾ and من الضالين its khabar, that is, [one of those who had gone astray] from what Allah gave me afterwards of knowledge and the message. He thereby held the station of prophethood above that attribute which Pharaoh had applied to him, namely his words to him وأنت من الكافرين, and so he said من الضالين, that is, those who err, like one who kills by mistake without intending to kill. (فَفَرَرْتُ مِنْكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْماً وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; فررت is a verb and agent; منكم is attached to فررت; لما is temporal, as al-Fārisī says, or a connective, as Sībawayh says, and the clause خفتكم is what the adverbial is annexed to; فوهب is conjoined to ففررت; لي is attached to وهب; ربي is the agent; حكما is the direct object; and وجعلني من المرسلين is conjoined to what precedes. By this statement he warded off the slur upon his prophethood, that is, the gift of judgement and prophethood came after that incident. Then he turned back on his reminder of the favour of rearing him, and refuted it, nullified it from its very root and tore it out from its foundation, with the words: (وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّها عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to demolish the accusation Pharaoh had directed at him. وتلك is a mubtadaʾ and نعمة its khabar; the clause تمنها is an adjective of نعمة; علي is attached to تمنها; and أن together with what is within its scope is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to تلك, because the demonstrative points to a hideous plan and an ugly trait whose reality cannot be grasped except through its explanation, so the explicative apposition came to explain what was left vague and to open what was closed. It is also permissible to parse the interpreted maṣdar as a badal (substitute) from نعمة, or as being in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). تمنها is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, because مَنَّ is an intransitive verb that is made transitive by the bāʾ, that is, "you bestow it upon me" (تمن بها).
Al-Jalāl [al-Suyūṭī] pointed out in his abridged tafsir that some scholars implied a hamza at the beginning of the sentence, that is, before وتلك, so that the original sentence is "أو تلك؟", meaning: "This is not a favour for you to remind me of it." The one who implied it is al-Akhfash. This hamza is for rebuking interrogation (istifhām inkārī) containing the sense of negation, as we have explained.

* Rhetoric:
Ambiguity (al-ibhām):
In his words «وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت» there is an ambiguity with no explanation. It is of two kinds: an ambiguity that is explained, and an ambiguity without explanation. His words «التي فعلت» send the imagination in every direction and bear many meanings, and this is frequent and widespread in the Noble Qur'an.

dervis-irab:23-31.t:
* I'rab:
(قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ: وَما رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ) قال فرعون is a verb and agent. The wāw is a conjunction, to conjoin the statement to Moses' statement «إنا رسول رب العالمين». ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and رب العالمين is its khabar. He answered with ما only because he was asking about His attributes and acts; had he wanted His very self, he would have said من ("who")? (قالَ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ) قال موسى: هو رب, so رب is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. وما is conjoined to the two genera, so no objection arises over the dual [in بينهما], which refers back to the plural. بينهما is an adverbial attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila. إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); it is kāna with its noun and predicate. The apodosis of إن is omitted, that is: "If you are among those from whom sound reflection and right consideration is expected, this answer will benefit you"; or you may imply: "If you are certain of anything, then this is the most deserving thing to be certain of, because of its clarity and the brilliance of its proof." (قالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُ أَلا تَسْتَمِعُونَ) قال فرعون; لمن is attached to قال; حوله is an adverbial attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila, and they are the nobles of his people; the hamza is interrogative and لا is negative; تستمعون is an imperfect verb and its agent, and its object is omitted, that is, his answer, which did not match the question. (قالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) قال موسى; وربكم is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is..." He was included and comprised within his words رب السموات والأرض وما بينهما, in order to provoke and defy him. The secret of mentioning the specific after the general will come in the chapter on rhetoric.
(قالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ) قال فرعون; the clause إن رسولكم is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إن with its noun; الذي is an adjective; the clause أرسل إليكم is the ṣila of the relative noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and مجنون is the khabar of إن. This is the way of the falsifiers and tyrants when they are left helpless: they resort to describing the possessor of the truth as mad or the like, because they have no proof with which to oppose him. (قالَ رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَما بَيْنَهُما إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ) قال موسى, to increase his provocation and to demonstrate his baseness: He is the Lord of the east and the west and what is between them. The secret of this antithesis (ṭibāq) will come in the chapter on rhetoric. وإن كنتم تعقلون is a condition whose apodosis is omitted, that is: "If you have a trace of reason, you would know that you have no answer other than stubbornness, folly and extravagance in speech." He said first إن كنتم موقنين because the situation was one of proof and persuasion; then, when he despaired and the obstinacy grew intense, he was harsh with them and met their obstinacy, and their ascribing madness to him, with the like of it, denying them the reason that would enable them to distinguish between things. (قالَ لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إِلهَاً غَيْرِي لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ الْمَسْجُونِينَ) قال فرعون; in لئن the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath, and إن is conditional; اتخذت is a past verb and agent, in the position of jussive as the protasis; إلها is the direct object; غيري is an adjective; the lām is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath, in accordance with the well-known rule. لأجعلنك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; من المسجونين is in the position of accusative as the second object. (قالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ مُبِينٍ) قال موسى; the hamza is interrogative and the wāw is a ḥāl-wāw. Every sentence of this construction is preceded by an omitted verb, that is: "Would you do that even if...". لو is conditional; جئتك is a past verb, agent and direct object; بشيء is attached to جئتك; and مبين is an adjective of شيء, that is, with a brilliant proof of my prophethood. (قالَ فَأْتِ بِهِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) قال فرعون; in فأت the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), that is, "if you are truthful in your claim, then bring it". به is attached to فأت; إن is conditional; كنت is the protasis; it is kāna with its noun; من الصادقين is the predicate of كنت; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
The general and the specific:
After mentioning the general in his words «رب السموات والأرض وما بينهما», by which he encompassed all creatures, he returned to specification by mentioning themselves and their forefathers, and the antithesis between the east and the west, so that they might reflect upon themselves; for the nearest thing for a rational being to contemplate is himself and those born of him, and the evidences of the Maker which he has seen and witnessed, and the transfer from one form to another and from one state to another from the time of his birth to the time of his death. He made the antithesis between the east and the west because the rising of the sun from one of the two horizons and its setting in the other, in a straight measure and a fixed order without defect throughout the seasons of the year, and by a straight reckoning too, is among the clearest things from which proof can be drawn.
Pharaoh generalised a second time by making him "of the imprisoned" and did not say "I will imprison you", to indicate that this was his habit: he would seize whom he wanted to imprison and cast him into a pit of deep bottom, alone, where he saw no light and heard no sound from outside, which was crueller than killing. This is the habit of the stubborn, arrogant one who is refuted, when the days favour him and time smiles upon him: when he comes to rule a land in a heedless moment of time, he believes that its people must worship him. The lām in من المسجونين is the lām of familiarity (lil-ʿahd), that is, "of those whose condition you have known and whose state you have been familiar with in my prisons". So generalisation here is more eloquent, just as specification in what preceded is more eloquent. How wonderful is the style of the Qur'an: it soars above shallow, primitive minds, and is subtle to the first, rudimentary understanding.

dervis-irab:90-104.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to «لا ينفع». He brought it in the past form only to indicate that its occurrence is certain: when Paradise draws near the standing-place of the blessed, they look at it and rejoice at the bliss that awaits them in it; and when the Fire draws near the standing-place of the wretched, they look at it and grieve that they are being driven to it. «أزلفت» is a past passive verb, meaning "was brought near"; «الجنة» is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «للمتقين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أزلفت». (وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِلْغاوِينَ) Conjoined to the preceding clause. (وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ؟) The wāw is a conjunction; «قيل» is a past passive verb; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قيل», that is, by way of rebuke. «أين» is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted predicate placed first (khabar muqaddam); «ما» is a relative noun, a delayed subject (mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar); the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila (relative clause) and the clause «تعبدون» is the khabar of «كنتم». (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ هَلْ يَنْصُرُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَنْتَصِرُونَ) «من دون الله» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «هل» is an interrogative particle; «ينصرونكم» is an imperfect verb with its agent and direct object; «أو» is a conjunction; «ينتصرون» is an imperfect verb with its agent. (فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيها هُمْ وَالْغاوُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «كبكبوا» is a passive verb, described in the source as "imperfect" (Translator's note: the source says «فعل مضارع مبني للمجهول»; the verb is in fact a past passive); the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); «الغاوون» is conjoined to the wāw in «كبكبوا», which is permitted by the separation made by the preposition and its genitive noun and the separating pronoun. (وَجُنُودُ إِبْلِيسَ أَجْمَعُونَ) «وجنود» is also conjoined to the wāw; «إبليس» is muḍāf ilayhi; «أجمعون» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the wāw and of what is conjoined to it. (قالُوا وَهُمْ فِيها يَخْتَصِمُونَ) «قالوا» is a verb and agent; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; «هم» is mubtadaʾ; «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يختصمون»; and the clause «يختصمون» is their khabar. The disputing is between the devils and those who followed them, so the pronoun refers back to «الغاوون».
(تَاللَّهِ إِنْ كُنَّا لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear", and it is attached to «قالوا». «إن» is the lightened form of the heavy «إنّ», and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), that is, "indeed it"; the clause «كنا» is the khabar of «إن»; «كان» and its noun; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); «في ضلال» is the khabar of «كنا» and «مبين» is an adjective. (إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ بِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) «إذ» is an adverb for past time, attached to «مبين» or to an omitted verb indicated by «ضلال»; it is not permissible for it to be attached to «ضلال», because a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has been qualified does not operate after the qualification. The imperfect form serves to make the past scene present to the mind. The meaning is: "By Allah, we were in the utmost manifest error at the time of our making you, O these idols, equal to the Lord of the worlds in deserving worship, while you are the lowliest and most helpless of creatures." (وَما أَضَلَّنا إِلَّا الْمُجْرِمُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction or a ḥāl wāw; «ما» is negative; «أضلنا» is a verb with a direct object placed first; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «المجرمون» is the agent of «أضلنا». They are their leaders and great ones, as He the Exalted said: «ربنا إننا أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا فأضلونا السبيلا».
(فَما لَنا مِنْ شافِعِينَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); «ما» is negative; «لنا» is a khabar placed first; «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; «شافعين» is genitive in form and nominative in position as a delayed subject. (Translator's note: the source says «خبرا مقدما», "a khabar placed first", for «شافعين»; it is written here as in the source.)
(وَلا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ) Conjoined to «شافعين»; «حميم» is an adjective of «صديق».
(فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; «لو» is a particle of wishing in a place like this, as if it were said "would that we had a return", because of the meeting point in meaning between «لو» and «ليت»; it may also be in its original sense as a conditional, with the apodosis omitted, its implied form being "we would have done such and such". «أن» is a particle resembling the verb; it and what is within its scope are the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "we wish", for which «لو» has stood in, or the agent of an omitted verb if «لو» is conditional. «لنا» is the advanced khabar of «أن» and «كرة» is the delayed noun of «أن»; the fāʾ in «فنكون» is the fāʾ of causation, and «نكون» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ; the noun of «نكون» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; «من المؤمنين» is the khabar of «نكون». (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) «إن», its advanced khabar and its delayed noun; «ما» is negative; «كان» with its noun and khabar.
(وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ) The wāw is resumptive; «إن» and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «هو» is a separating pronoun or a mubtadaʾ; «العزيز» is the khabar of «إن» or the khabar of «هو»; «الرحيم» is a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «فكبكبوا فيها هم والغاوون» there is the strength of the expression for the strength of the meaning. This is among the points on which Ibn Jinnī alone drew attention in the book «al-Khaṣāʾiṣ». For «kabkaba» is the repetition of «kabb» (casting down on one's face); the repetition in the wording was made an indication of repetition in the meaning, as if, when he is thrown into Hell, he is tumbled again and again until he settles at its bottom. Yet an increase in wording does not indicate strength of meaning in a consistent way; rather the matter depends on taste. Take as an example the added diminutive: it is an increase that reduces, so «rujayl» is less than «rajul» in meaning, though it has more letters.
2- Clarification (al-īḍāḥ):
It has been mentioned often: the speaker mentions words that on the surface contain an ambiguity, then clarifies it in the rest of his speech. The difficulty that clarification resolves occurs in the meanings of rare expressions, in their i'rab, and in the meanings of the soul rather than the arts. Here it is in His saying «ولا صديق حميم»: the friend described by the attribute «ḥamīm» is the one who surpasses kinship and exceeds it in being a «ḥamīm». «Ḥamīm» is from «iḥtimām», which is concern, that is, our affair concerns him and his affair concerns us. It is also said to be from «ḥāmma», which is the inner circle, from their saying "the ḥāmma of so-and-so", that is, his intimates.

dervis-irab:105-122.t:
* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) A resumptive statement, brought to begin the narration of the third story. «كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين»: verb, agent and direct object. The verb is feminine in view of the meaning of «القوم», which is the nation and the group. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«al-qawm» is used as masculine and feminine, so one says «qāma al-qawm» and «qāmat al-qawm»; likewise every collective noun that has no singular from its own wording, such as «rahṭ» and «nafar»." In al-Zamakhsharī and al-Bayḍāwī: "«al-qawm» is feminine, and therefore its diminutive is «quwayma»", and this is taken as referring to the most common usage. If you ask: how did He say "the people of Noah denied the messengers" when they denied only Noah alone? I say: it is like their saying "So-and-so rides the beasts and wears the cloaks" when he has only one beast and one cloak. (إِذْ قالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلا تَتَّقُونَ) The adverb is attached to «كذبت»; the clause «قال» is in the position of the genitive because the adverb is annexed to it; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قال»; «أخوهم» is the agent of «قال» and «نوح» is a badal (substitute). He called him their brother only following their manner of speech, as in their saying "O brother of the Arabs" and "O brother of Tamīm", meaning "O one of them". Of this is the verse in al-Ḥamāsa:
لا يسألون أخاهم حين يندبهم ... في النائبات على ما قال برهانا
(They do not ask their brother, when he summons them in calamities, for proof of what he said.)
«ألا» is a particle of offering; «تتقون» is an imperfect verb and agent. (إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ) A justification for his offering them the inclination towards piety. «إن» and its noun; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) or to «رسول»; «رسول» is the khabar and «أمين» is an adjective. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; «اتقوا الله»: imperative verb, agent and direct object; «أطيعون»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أطيعون» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent, the nūn is the protective nūn, and the omitted yāʾ, omitted to keep the verse endings, is the direct object.
(وَما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «أسألكم» is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and «أجر» is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a direct object; «إن» is negative; «أجري» is mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «على رب العالمين» is the khabar. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) Its i'rab was given just above. The five stories were opened with the command to piety to indicate that the heavenly religions agree on the obligation of knowing the truth and following it, and the very same sentence was repeated as emphasis of this lofty aim. (قالُوا: أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَاتَّبَعَكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ) The hamza is for an interrogative of denial; «نؤمن» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "we"; «لك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نؤمن»; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; «اتبعك الأرذلون» is a verb, direct object and agent. The ḥāl wāw here ought to have «qad» implied after it. This is a kind of foolishness: they measure the worthiness of followers by the amount of wealth and goods they enjoy, or by the lineage and standing by which they are distinguished, but Islam made all Muslims equal. (قالَ وَما عِلْمِي بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; «ما» may be interrogative or negative. On the first, it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ and «علمي» is its khabar, and «بما» is attached to «علمي» in every case; on making it negative, the khabar is omitted so that the speech becomes a clause with it. The clause «كانوا» is the ṣila of «ما» and the clause «يعملون» is the khabar of «كانوا». (إِنْ حِسابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّي لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ) «إن» is negative; «حسابهم» is mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «على ربي» is the khabar of «حسابهم»; «لو» is a particle of prevention (imtināʿiyya); «تشعرون» is an imperfect nominative verb. The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, just as the object of «تشعرون» is omitted, its implied form being "that"; the implied apodosis is "you would not have faulted them, nor ascribed any deficiency to them". (وَما أَنَا بِطارِدِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is the Ḥijāzī «mā»; «أنا» is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; «طارد» is genitive in form, and in position the khabar of «ما»; «المؤمنين» is muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنْ أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) «إن» is negative; «أنا» is mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «نذير» is the khabar and «مبين» an adjective. (قالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يا نُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمَرْجُومِينَ) The lām is the preparatory lām of the oath; «إن» is conditional; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «تنته» is an imperfect verb, jussive by «لم», and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; in «لتكونن» the lām is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted according to the well-known rule:
واحذف لدى اجتماع شرط وقسم ... جواب ما أخرت فهو ملتزم
(Omit, when a condition and an oath come together, the answer of whichever you put later; that is binding.)
«تكونن» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the noun of «تكونن» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and «من المرجومين» is the khabar.
(قالَ: رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي كَذَّبُونِ) «رب» is the one addressed (vocative), annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the vocative particle is omitted; «إن» and its noun; the clause «كذبون» is its khabar, and «كذبون» is a past verb, agent and direct object; the first-person yāʾ was omitted to keep the verse endings. (فَافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحاً وَنَجِّنِي وَمَنْ مَعِيَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; «افتح» is an imperative verb whose meaning is supplication, and its agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; «بيني» is an adverb attached to «افتح»; «بينهم» is conjoined to «بيني»; «فتحا» may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and may be a direct object. «al-Fatḥ» here is from «al-fatāḥa» in the sense of judgment, and «al-fattāḥ» is the judge, so called for his opening the locks of affairs. In al-Qāmūs: "«al-fatāḥa», with ḍamma and kasra; it is said «baynahumā fatāḥāt», that is, disputes." The meaning is: "judge between us as each of us deserves"; what is meant is "send down punishment upon them", and therefore he said «ونجني». «ونجني»: the wāw is a conjunction and «نجني» is conjoined to «احكم»; «ومن»: the wāw is a conjunction or of accompaniment, and «من» is conjoined to the yāʾ or is an object of accompaniment; «معي» is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of «من»; «من المؤمنين» is a ḥāl. (فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and this is of the speech of the Exalted; «أنجيناه» is a past verb, agent and direct object; «من» is an object of accompaniment or conjoined to the hāʾ; «معه» is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; «في الفلك» is attached to the "being-in-place" to which the adverb is attached; «المشحون» is an adjective of «الفلك», and «al-mashḥūn» means "filled".
(ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنا بَعْدُ الْباقِينَ) «ثم» is a conjunction of delay; «أغرقنا» is a verb and agent; «بعد» is an adverb of time, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, the meaning being "after their rescue"; «الباقين» is the direct object of «أغرقنا». (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) A resumptive statement to show the lesson of this story. «إن» is a particle resembling the verb; «في ذلك» is an advanced khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; «آية» is the delayed noun of «إن»; the wāw is a conjunction or a ḥāl wāw; «ما» is negative; «كان» with its noun; «مؤمنين» is its khabar. He means that their overwhelming majority did not believe, and therefore they were seized; had even half of them at least been believers, they would have been saved. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; the shifted lām; «هو» is a separating pronoun or a mubtadaʾ; «العزيز» is the khabar of «إن» or of «هو»; «الرحيم» is a second khabar. The i'rab of its like has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
The repetition in His saying «فاتقوا الله وأطيعون» is for emphasis and for fixing the matter in the souls, even though each of the two was tied to a reason: the first to trustworthiness, the second to the cutting off of covetousness. Its like is your saying: "Do you not fear Allah in my disobedience, when I raised you as a small child? Do you not fear Allah in my disobedience, when I taught you as a grown one?"
In it there is also advancing (taqdīm): the command to fear Allah is put before the command to obey him, because fear of Allah is the reason for obeying him.

dervis-irab:32-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ثُعْبانٌ): The thuʿbān is the snake; the word is used for both male and female, and its plural is thaʿābīn. The derivation of thuʿbān is from thaʿaba al-māʾ, "he made the water flow", so it flowed (inthaʿaba). This "thuʿbān-ness" appeared in the staff when he threw it down. The letter thāʾ with ʿayn in particular carries the senses of colour-changing, guile and pouring forth. One says thaʿʿa yathiʿʿu (of the pattern ḍaraba) thaʿʿan, "he vomited what he had eaten"; inthaʿʿa al-akl min fīhi, "the food poured from his mouth", and "the blood from his nose or his wound", that is, it gushed. Among their sayings: sāla al-thuʿbān, "the thuʿbān flowed", as the thuʿbān flows; thuʿbān is a plural of thaʿb, which is a watercourse. He said:
وما ثعب باتت تطرّده الصبا ... بسرّاء واد منجد غير اتهما
(Gloss: Not a watercourse which the east wind drove on all night, in the best part of a valley, high and not low-lying...)
Figuratively: ṣāḥa bihi fa-inthaʿaba ilayhi, "he shouted at him and he leapt running towards him"; and shadd athʿūb, "a gushing run". He said:
لها إذا حرّ الحرار واللوب ... قوائم «عوج» وشدّ أثعوب
(Gloss: When the heat of the lava-fields and the black stony ground blazes, she has [crooked] legs and a gushing run.)
And Abū Duʾād said:
وكل قائمة تهوي لوجهتها ... لها أتي كفرغ الدلو أثعوب
(Gloss: Every one standing, swooping towards her direction, has a rushing stream like the pouring of a bucket, gushing.)
Both [usages] are from the category of metaphor, though the route is different. Thaʿaba ʿalayhim al-ghāra means "he launched the raid against them"; thaʿaba al-baʿīr shaqshaqatahu means "the camel brought out its throat-sac". Thaʿilat asnānuhu, taṯʿalu (of the pattern fataḥa), thaʿalan: his teeth overlapped, one upon the other, and he is athʿal; and it carries the sense of colour-changing and guile. Athʿala al-amr means "the matter became great and grew serious". Al-thuʿal (with a ḍamma on the thāʾ, described in the source as «المشددة», "doubled") [Translator's note: translated as written; the source's description of the thāʾ as doubled is unclear] is a small creature that appears in the water-skin when its smell turns foul. Thuʿāla is a proper name for a female fox and is diptote. Thaʿlaba and tathaʿlaba: he swerved, or imitated the fox in its swerving. The thaʿlab is an animal famed for guile and swerving, whose hair falls out each year; hence dāʾ al-thaʿlab, "fox disease", which is the process of hair falling out. The female is called thaʿlaba and the male thuʿlubān; the word thaʿlab applies to both masculine and feminine, and its plural is thaʿālib and thaʿāl. The thaʿlab is also the end of the spear that goes into the socket of the spearhead. Bashshār said:
وجيش كجنح الليل يزحف بالحصى ... وبالشوك والخطي حصر ثعالبه
(Gloss: An army like a wing of the night, advancing with pebbles and thorns, and with Khaṭṭī spears whose spear-ends are constricted.)
The thaʿlaba is also the coccyx and the anus. In sum, this root is evident in both "fox-ness" and "snake-ness".
(أَرْجِهْ): and arjiʾhu, as it was also read with the hamza and with the lightened form; they are two dialects. One says arjaʾtuhu and arjaytuhu when you put it off; from it comes al-Murjiʾa.

* I'rab:
