They would go in to the woman in her curtained chamber and say, "Do you agree?" and she would say, "Yes", and likewise their children.
Qudār became a proverb for ill omen. Zuhayr alluded to him, but erred, making him the "red one of ʿĀd" when he is the red one of Thamūd, in verses of his in which he describes war and warns his people of its evil results. We give them here in full because of their importance:
وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم ... وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم
(War is nothing but what you know and have tasted; it is not a matter of conjecture and hearsay.)
متى تبعثوها تبعثوها ذميمة ... وتضر إذا ضرّيتموها فتضرم
(When you rouse it, you rouse it hateful; and it grows fierce when you make it fierce, and it blazes.)
فتعرككم عرك الرحى بثفالها ... وتلقح كشافا ثم تنتج فتئثم
(It will grind you as the millstone grinds with its padding; it conceives, being mounted again, then bears, and bears twins.)
فتنتج لكم غلمان أشأم كلهم ... كأحمر عاد ثم ترضع فتفطم
(It will bear you boys, every one of them more ill-omened than the red one of ʿĀd; then it suckles, and weans.)
That is, it bears you sons, each of whom matches in ill omen the hamstringer of the she-camel, who is Qudār ibn Sālif.

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(باخِعٌ): the explanation of this word has already been given. Al-bakhʿ is for the slaughtering to reach the bukhāʿ (with a bāʾ), which is a vein running inside the vertebrae, and that is the furthest limit for the slaughterer. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "bakhaʿa nafsahu bakhʿan (from the pattern of nafaʿa): he killed himself out of grief or rage; and bakhaʿa lī bi-l-ḥaqq bukhūʿan: he submitted to it and gave it up."

* I'rab:
(طسم، تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ): the parsing of «طسم» and the discussion of the openings of the suras have already been given. «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ, «آيات الكتاب» its khabar, and «المبين» an adjective of «كتاب».
(لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ): «لعل» is for solicitude, that is, the hope here is in the sense of a command: have mercy on yourself and be gentle with it. The kāf is its noun, «باخع» its khabar, and «نفسك» a direct object of «باخع». «أن» and what is within its scope is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is, for fear that they will not believe, or because of their not believing; «مؤمنين» is the khabar of «يكونوا».
(إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْناقُهُمْ لَها خاضِعِينَ): resumptive discourse, introduced to give the reason for the command that he be solicitous toward himself over giving way to grief and distress at their not believing. «إن» is conditional; «نشأ» is the protasis and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; the object of the willing is omitted because it is the content of the apodosis, that is, "their belief"; «ننزل» is the apodosis; «عليهم» is attached to «ننزل»; «من السماء» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «آية». The fāʾ is a conjunction; «ظلت» is a defective past verb conjoined to «ننزل», so it is jussive in position. It is permissible that the fāʾ be resumptive and «ظلت» be in the sense of the imperfect, that is, "continue to remain", and to this al-Jalāl inclined, so he explained it as nominative [Translator's note: i.e. as "will remain"]. «أعناقهم» is the noun of «ظلت»; «لها» is attached to «خاضعين»; «خاضعين» is the khabar of «ظلت». The secret of the difference in conjunction and the secret of «خاضعين» coming as a khabar of «الأعناق» will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَما يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنَ الرَّحْمنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كانُوا عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «يأتيهم» is an imperfect verb and direct object; «من» is a redundant preposition, and «ذكر» is genitive in form and nominative in position, because it is the agent of «يأتيهم»; «من الرحمن» is an adjective of «ذكر», and «محدث» a second adjective, that is, its sending down is renewed according to the requirements of circumstances; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; the clause «كانوا» is an exception from the most general of circumstances, so it is a ḥāl; «كان» and its noun; «عنه» is attached to «معرضين»; and «معرضين» is the khabar of «كانوا». (فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنْبؤُا ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, as if it were said: if you wish to know what their position was toward the reminder when they turned away from it and averted from pondering it, then they have denied.
«قد» is a particle of affirmation; «كذبوا» is a past verb and agent; «فسيأتيهم» is conjoined to what precedes, as a threat and warning; «يأتيهم» is an imperfect verb and direct object; «أنباء» is the agent; «ما» is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «كانوا» is the ṣila; the wāw is the noun of «كان»; «به» is attached to «يستهزئون»; and the clause «يستهزئون» is the khabar of «كانوا». (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنْبَتْنا فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ): the hamza is for rhetorical interrogation, and the wāw is a conjunction on something implied; such an expression has often preceded. «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; «يروا» is an imperfect verb jussive by «لم», and the wāw is the agent. The seeing here is by sight, and for that reason it was made transitive by «إلى»; «إلى الأرض» is attached to «يروا»; «كم» is exclamatory (khabariyya) in the position of accusative as the object of «أنبتنا»; «أنبتنا» is a verb and agent; «من كل زوج» is the tamyīz of the exclamatory «كم», and it may be a ḥāl, as Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned; «كريم» is an adjective of «زوج». By «زوج» He meant the kind and species of plant, and further discussion of it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): «إن» is a particle resembling the verb; «في ذلك» is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «آية» is the noun of «إن». «وما»: the wāw is a ḥāl-wāw and «ما» is negative; «كان أكثرهم مؤمنين»: kāna with its noun and khabar, that is, that was foreknown in Allah's knowledge. Sībawayh said «كان» is redundant, and further discussion of this will come in the section on Benefits. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ): the wāw is resumptive; «إن» and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; «العزيز» is the khabar of «إن» or the khabar of «هو», the clause being the khabar of «إن»; and «الرحيم» is a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
These verses contain many arts of rhetoric, which we list below:
1- Variation in conjunction:
He varied in the conjunction, conjoining «فظلت» to «ننزل». Had it been said «أنزلنا» it would have been correct, and perhaps the context required it, but it was varied because conjoining the past to the future gives a sense of its realisation and that it will certainly come to be, for the past verb indicates the occurrence of the act and its being decided. It has parallels in the Qur'an which will come in their places.
2- Rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī):
There is a rational trope in attributing submission to the necks. It may be asked: how is it right that «خاضعين» comes as a khabar of «الأعناق», when submission is a characteristic of rational beings? The original wording was «فظلوا لها خاضعين». The secret in that is that when they were described with submission, which belongs to rational beings, it was said «خاضعين», as preceded in His saying «لي ساجدين». There are other views, which the scholars of bayān brought to seven, and we summarise them as follows:
a- What is meant is the leaders, as they are called "faces" and "chests".
b- That it is on omission of a muḍāf, that is, "so the owners of the necks remained", then it was omitted and the khabar stayed as it was before the omission, out of regard for the omitted.
c- That when it was annexed to rational beings, it acquired this rule from them, as femininity is acquired through annexation.
d- That aʿnāq is the plural of ʿunuq in the sense of a group of people; one says "a ʿunuq of people came to us", that is, a company; the well-known limb is not meant.
e- The insertion of the necks to show the place of submission, leaving the speech as it was.
[Translator's note: the source then has an unlettered sentence, apparently the sixth view, which is the next sentence: ] And what he mentioned is that they were treated as rational beings when what is ordinarily among the acts of rational beings was attributed to them, by way of rational trope.
ز- That when He annexed the necks to the masculine, the necks being joined to them in creation and formation, their rule was applied to them. [Translator's note: the lettering in the source skips from هـ to ز; the sixth item has no letter.]
From Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with both: This verse was revealed about us and about Banū Umayya. He said: "The dominion will be ours over them, and their necks will humble themselves to us after hardness, and abasement will overtake them after might."
3- Completion (tatmīm):
By His saying «أولم يروا إلى الأرض كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم». It would have sufficed to say "how many We caused to grow in it of noble kinds". What is the meaning of combining kam and kull? The answer is that kull was introduced only to encompass the kinds of plants, while kam indicated that this encompassed quantity is excessive in multitude, and by that there is a warning of the completeness and perfection of power. This is the requirement of tatmīm, to which reference has previously been made, and its definition is:
that a word is brought in speech which, if dropped from the speech, its meaning would be deficient in itself or in its attributes while its wording is complete; just as what is intended here in the verse is the individual units of kinds. This is indicated by the fact that if "kull" were dropped and you said: "Look at the earth, how many Allah has caused to grow in it of such-and-such kind," you would be alluding to the individuals of that kind referred to; but if you bring in kull, you have, by repeating it, covered the individuals of every kind, not the individuals of a specific kind.
4- Also tatmīm:
He also completed by describing the pair (zawj) as noble (karīm), and that is for two matters:
a- That plants, as is known, are of two kinds, beneficial and harmful; so by the word karīm it denotes that He means the beneficial kind, so He mentioned the multitude of what He caused to grow in the earth of all kinds of beneficial plants and left the harmful out of the mention.
b- That He means both kinds, the beneficial and the harmful, and describes them all as noble, as a warning that He created nothing except for a benefit, though its secrets may be hidden from you and hard for you to fathom; but He, the Exalted, knows what you do not know.

dervis-irab:160-175.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الذُّكْرانَ): One of the plurals of «dhakar»; «al-dhakar» is the opposite of the female. In al-Mukhtār: "«Al-dhakar» is the opposite of the female, and its plural is «dhukūr», «dhukrān» and «dhakāra», like «ḥijāra»." In al-Qāmūs many plurals are given for it: "Its plural is «dhukūr», «dhukūra», «dhukrān», «dhikār», «dhikāra» and «dhikara»."
(الْقالِينَ): Those who hate. «Al-qilā» is intense hatred, as if it were a hatred that roasts the heart and the liver. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«Qalaytu al-rajul aqlīhi», of the pattern «ramā», with «qilā» with kasra and shortened, and sometimes lengthened, means I hated him; and in a dialect, of the pattern «taʿiba»." The wording of al-Qāmūs: "«Qalāhu», like «ramāhu» and «raḍiyahu», «qilan», «qilāʾan» and «maqliyya»: he hated him and disliked him with utmost dislike, and so left him; or «qalāhu» in forsaking and «qaliyahu» in hatred."
(الْغابِرِينَ): He said in al-Kashshāf: "The meaning of «al-ghābirīn» in the punishment and destruction: those who were not saved." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«Ghabara ghubūran», of the pattern «qaʿada», means he remained; it is sometimes used for what has passed also, and so is among the contronyms (aḍdād). Al-Zubaydī said: «ghabara ghubūran» means he stayed; and in one dialect it is with the unpointed letter (ʿ-b-r) for the past and with the pointed (gh-b-r) for what remains; and «ghubbar al-shayʾ», of the pattern «sukkar», is its remainder." In al-Qāmūs: "«Ghabara ghubūran» means he stayed and he went, a contronym; he is «ghābir», from «ghubbar», like «rukkaʿ»; and «ghubr al-shayʾ», with ḍamma, is its remainder."

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) A resumptive clause, brought to begin the sixth story. (إِذْ قالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلا تَتَّقُونَ) Lot was not their brother by lineage; he called him their brother only following their manner of speech, as earlier, or in view of his dwelling beside them and neighbouring them in their town. (إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ، فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ، وَما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) He opened every story with these verses and their i'rab has been given, so this renews the covenant with it. (أَتَأْتُونَ الذُّكْرانَ مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of denial and rebuke; «تأتون الذكران»: imperfect verb, agent and direct object; the position of the rebuking interrogative clause is the accusative as a ḥāl; and «من العالمين» is a ḥāl. (وَتَذَرُونَ ما خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ عادُونَ) «وتذرون» is conjoined to «تأتون», within the scope of the rebuking interrogative; it is an imperfect verb and agent; «ما» is the direct object; the clause «خلق لكم ربكم» is the ṣila; «من أزواجكم» is a ḥāl, taking «من» as explanatory, and it may also be partitive; the detail of all this will come in the section of Rhetoric. «بل» is a particle of transitional turning away; «أنتم» is mubtadaʾ; «قوم» is the khabar and «عادون» an adjective, that is, those who overstep the lawful to the unlawful, because the meaning of «al-ʿādī» is the one who transgresses in his wrongdoing, exceeding the limit in it. (قالُوا: لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يا لُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُخْرَجِينَ) «قالوا» is a past verb and agent; «لئن»: the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath and «إن» is conditional; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «تنته» is an imperfect verb, jussive by «لم»; «لتكونن»: the lām falls in the answer of the oath; «تكونن» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the (elided) wāw is the noun of «تكونن» (Translator's note: the source says «والواو اسم تكونن», though the verb is second person singular and its noun is a latent pronoun, "you"; it is translated as written); «من المخرجين» is the khabar, that is, "of the number of those whom we have expelled". A detailed discussion of this expression will come in the section of Rhetoric. (قالَ إِنِّي لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِنَ الْقالِينَ) «إن» and its noun; «لعملكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «القالين»; «من القالين» is the khabar of «إن», and the clause is the content of the saying. Some were strict and said, in the glosses on al-Bayḍāwī, the following: "«من القالين» is attached to an omitted word, that is, «laqālin min al-qālīn», and that omitted word is the khabar of «إن», and «من القالين» is an adjective, and «لعملكم» is attached to the omitted khabar; for if «من القالين» were made the khabar of «إن», the «qālīn» would operate in «لعملكم», which leads to putting the object of the ṣila before the relative noun, which is «al», though that is not permissible." I say: this, for all its precision and suitability to the rules, involves great artificiality that takes it to the impossible, and there is no call for this strictness, given that the use of «al» as a relative is almost rare.
(رَبِّ نَجِّنِي وَأَهْلِي مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ) «رب» is the one addressed, annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the vocative particle is omitted from it; «نجني» is an imperative verb of supplication and the yāʾ is the direct object; «أهلي» is an object of accompaniment or conjoined to the yāʾ; «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نجني», and the clause «يعملون» is the ṣila of «ما». (فَنَجَّيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction on an implied omitted element so that the story is coherent; «نجيناه» is a past verb, agent and direct object; «أهله» is an object of accompaniment or conjoined to the hāʾ; «أجمعين» is emphasis. (إِلَّا عَجُوزاً فِي الْغابِرِينَ) «إلا» is a particle of exception; «عجوزا» is the excepted by «إلا», and she is his wife; «في الغابرين» is an adjective of «عجوزا», as if it were said "except an old woman who remained behind". (ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا الْآخَرِينَ) Conjoined to what precedes. (وَأَمْطَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَراً فَساءَ مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ) «وأمطرنا» is conjoined to «دمرنا»; «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أمطرنا»; «مطرا» is the direct object; in «فساء» the fāʾ is a conjunction and «ساء» is a verb of dispraise; «مطر المنذرين» is the agent of «ساء»; and the one specified for dispraise is omitted, being «their rain». What is meant by the rain is the stones that poured down upon them. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) «إن», its advanced khabar and its delayed noun; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; «ما» is negative; «كان» with its noun and khabar.
(وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ) Its i'rab has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
1- His saying «وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم»: in this verse there is vagueness (ibhām) in His saying «ما خلق لكم», by which He intended their wives' fronts, and in that there is regard for modesty and discretion. «من» may be explanatory and may be partitive.
2- Turning to the adjective (al-ʿudūl ilā al-ṣifa):
In His saying «لتكونن من المخرجين» and His saying «من القالين» there is a turning from the verbal clause to the adjective. Often in the Qur'an, especially in this form, there is a turning from expression by the verb to expression by the derived adjective, and then making the one described by it one of a group, as in Pharaoh's saying «لأجعلنك من المسجونين»; examples are many. The secret in this is that expression by the verb conveys only the occurrence, whereas expression by the adjective, and then making the one described by it one of a group, conveys something beyond the occurrence: that the mentioned adjective is like a mark of the one described, firmly attached to him, as if it were a title, and as if he belonged to a class that has become of this specific kind, famed for some bad marks. Listen to the saying of the Exalted «رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف», how He attached to them a bad title and made them of a base kind famed for the mark of lagging behind, until it became a title clinging to it. This is general in all that comes to you and in what has passed of such examples; so reflect on it and give it its due.

dervis-irab:69-89.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْراهِيمَ) The wāw is a conjunction; اتل is conjoined to the implied اذكر ("remember"), which governs the words «وإذ نادى ربك موسى», to begin the second story; عليهم is attached to اتل; and نبأ إبراهيم is the direct object. (إِذْ قالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ ما تَعْبُدُونَ) إذ is an adverbial for past time and is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from نبأ, so its governor is اتل; it is also said that it is accusative by نبأ إبراهيم, that is, "at the time of his saying to his father and his people: What do you worship?" The clause قال is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; لأبيه is attached to قال, and لقومه is conjoined to it; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object of تعبدون; and the clause ما تعبدون is the content of the saying.
(قالُوا نَعْبُدُ أَصْناماً فَنَظَلُّ لَها عاكِفِينَ) The clause نعبد أصناما is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying; in فنظل the fāʾ is a conjunction and نظل is a defective imperfect verb whose noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; لها is attached to عاكفين and عاكفين is the khabar of نظل. In the speech there is an amplification (iṭnāb) which will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (قالَ: هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ) هل is a particle of interrogation; يسمعونكم is an imperfect verb and agent and the kāf is the direct object. An omitted element must be implied, that is, "they hear your supplication", so that it is transitive to one object, or "they hear you supplicating", so that it is transitive to two, the implied clause having stood in the place of the second object. إذ is an adverbial attached to يسمعونكم and, as al-Zamakhsharī says, it is for narrating a past state; its meaning is: "Call to mind the states in which you used to call upon them: did they hear you when you called?" This is more forceful in rebuking. The clause تدعون is genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it.
(أَوْ يَنْفَعُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ) Conjoined to يسمعونكم. (قالُوا بَلْ وَجَدْنا آباءَنا كَذلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ) بل is a transitional particle of retraction (iḍrāb intiqālī), by which they avoided answering his question, as though they found themselves in truth far removed from thinking and questioning, and that they had never returned to their reason to examine what they worship: does it hear? does it benefit? does it harm? It is merely imitation upon which they proceeded, without reflecting on its outcome or looking at its consequences and results. وجدنا is a verb and agent; آباءنا is the first object of وجدنا; the clause يفعلون is the second object; and كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "they do an act like that"; or the kāf may be made a fronted direct object of يفعلون, and this is perhaps preferable. (قالَ أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation, containing the sense of mockery and ridicule. It has already been mentioned that «رأيتم» in an expression like this is either in the sense of "tell me", being transitive to two objects, the first the relative noun and the second omitted, being a clause whose implied form is "is it worthy of worship?"; or else raʾā is in the sense of "he knew", and it takes one object, the meaning being "have you reflected and come to know what you used to worship?". The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element as we have implied, and many parallels of it have gone before in a construction like this. The clause كنتم is the ṣila of ما and the clause تعبدون is the khabar of كنتم. (أَنْتُمْ وَآباؤُكُمُ الْأَقْدَمُونَ) أنتم is an emphasis of the pronoun in تعبدون; آباؤكم is conjoined to أنتم; and الأقدمون is an adjective of آباؤكم. (فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ) The fāʾ is explanatory of cause; إن with its noun; عدو is its khabar; لي is an adjective of عدو. ʿAduww and ṣadīq come in the sense of singular and plural. He said:
وقوم عليّ ذوي مئرة ... أراهم عدوّا وكانوا صديقا
(Gloss: Many a people hostile to me, possessing fierce contention; I see them as enemies, though they were friends.)
It is also reported with the kasra [maʾra], which is strength and intensity of disputation, and al-maʾra is hostility.
He says: many a people, possessed of strength against me, I see today as enemies, though they were friends.
إلا is a particle of exception, and رب is accusative as the excepted. The exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), and for that reason إلا is implied in the sense of لكن ("but"). In the verse there is the art of allusion (taʿrīḍ), which will come in the chapter on rhetoric.
(الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ) الذي may be accusative as an adjective of رب العالمين, or as a badal or ʿaṭf bayān; or nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is the One who created me". Abū al-Baqāʾ erred, for he parsed الذي as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause هو يهدين and did not speak of the fāʾ; this is rejected, because the relative noun is specific, not general, and because the ṣila cannot admit renewal, so it is not like the conditional. The correct view is that it is resumptive, هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يهديني its khabar, and the yāʾ was dropped to observe the verse-endings (fawāṣil). (وَالَّذِي هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِي وَيَسْقِينِ) Conjoined to what went before; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يطعمني its khabar. (وَإِذا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ) The wāw is a conjunction; مرضت is a verb and agent. He ascribed the illness to himself, though illness and healing are from Allah the Exalted, out of courtesy, as al-Khiḍr said «فأردت أن أعيبها» and said «فأراد ربك أن يبلغا أشدهما»; further discussion on this point will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَالَّذِي يُمِيتُنِي ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ) Conjoined to what went before. The conjoining of يحيين to يميتني with ثم, contrary to what preceded, is because of the lapse of time and the breadth of the matter between the causing of death and the giving of life in the Hereafter. (وَالَّذِي أَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ) والذي is conjoined to what precedes; the clause أطمع is the ṣila; أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "in that He forgive"; لي is attached to يغفر; خطيئتي is the object of يغفر; and يوم الدين is an adverbial also attached to يغفر. (رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْماً وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ) رب is a vocative annexed to the first-person yāʾ, with the vocative particle omitted from it; هب is an imperative by which he meant supplication; لي is attached to هب; حكما is the direct object; وألحقني is conjoined to هب; and بالصالحين is attached to ألحقني. (وَاجْعَلْ لِي لِسانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ) واجعل is conjoined to what precedes; لي is the second object of اجعل; لسان صدق is the first object of اجعل, and the annexation is the annexation of the described to its description; and في الآخرين is a ḥāl, that is, those who come after me until the Day of Resurrection.
(وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ) من ورثة is the second object of اجعلني, and جنة النعيم is annexed to ورثة. (وَاغْفِرْ لِأَبِي إِنَّهُ كانَ مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ) لأبي is attached to اغفر; the clause إنه is a justification of the request for forgiveness for him; إن with its noun, the clause كان its khabar, and من الضالين the khabar of كان. (وَلا تُخْزِنِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ) The adverbial is attached to تخزني, and the clause يبعثون is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it.
(يَوْمَ لا يَنْفَعُ مالٌ وَلا بَنُونَ) يوم is an adverbial in the position of accusative, a badal from the first يوم; this confirms that it is from the speech of Abraham. It is also possible that it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted on this day, and there is no objection to parsing it as a badal also, that is, attached to what the first adverbial is attached to; the clause لا ينفع مال is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; and ولا بنون is conjoined to مال. (إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ) In this exception it is permissible that it be disjoined, that is, not of the same genus, its meaning being "but he who comes to Allah"; and it is permissible that it be connected (muttaṣil), and in that are two aspects. One is that it be a badal from the omitted element or an exception from it, so it is in the position of accusative on both aspects, the implication being "neither wealth nor sons benefit anyone except him who comes". It is also permissible that it be a badal from an agent, so that it is in the position of nominative, the rational being given priority, and the implication being "except the wealth of one who, and the sons of one who, for it benefits himself or another". Al-Zamakhsharī made من the object of ينفع, that is, "that does not benefit except a man who comes to Allah". بقلب is attached to أتى or to an omitted element as a ḥāl, that is, "accompanied by"; and سليم is an adjective of قلب.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there is a peerless loftiness from the standpoint of expressive rhetoric, before which necks are cut off and tongues fall silent. We shall incline to brevity, for there is room for speech here that the breadth of this book is too narrow to hold.

1- Amplification (al-iṭnāb):
- In his words: «قالوا نعبد أصناما فنظل لها عاكفين». What the answer to the question «ما تعبدون» required was that they say "idols", because it is a question about the object of worship only, like the words of the Exalted «ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون؟ قل العفو» and «ماذا قال ربكم؟ قالوا الحق». But they added to the answer an addition by which they explained their whole story, because they intended to show their delight and proclaim their pride. This is common in speech: you say to someone "What are you wearing?", and he says:
ألبس البرد الأتحمي فأجر أذياله بين جواري الحي الحسان
(Gloss: I wear the Atḥamī cloak and trail its hems among the beautiful girls of the tribe.)
They said «نظل» because they used to devote themselves to worshipping them by day and not by night. This is the merit of iṭnāb: it adds to the expression beyond the meaning for an intended benefit or a purposed end; when there is no benefit in the addition of wording, it is a wearisome prolixity, plainly insipid and manifestly weak.
2- Allusion (al-taʿrīḍ):
That is in his words «فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين». He pictured the matter in himself, with enmity aimed at his own person, as though alluding to them, saying: "I have thought about the matter at length and examined it closely, and I saw that my worship of them is worship of the enemy who lies in wait for him with misfortunes in order to bring him down. When a man reaches such a degree of baseness that he loves an enemy and prefers him with worship, that is plunging into the slippery places of error and the abysses of misguidance." Allusion may reach the one being advised in a way that plain statement does not, because it draws his attention and catches his eyes, so he reflects on it, and perhaps reflection leads him to acceptance. Among this is what is related of al-Shāfiʿī: a man confronted him with something and he said to him: "If you were where you are [in your position], you would need good manners."
3- The secrets of the conjunctions:
Here is a place of subtle approach and delicate aim which hardly anyone notices or any writer perceives. Most people place the conjunctions in the wrong places, so they make what should be governed by «على» governed by «في» among prepositions, just as they conjoin without being aware of the secret of the particle with which the speech was conjoined. The Exalted said «والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين، وإذا مرضت فهو يشفين، والذي يميتني ثم يحيين». The first He conjoined with the wāw, which is for mere combination, and putting feeding before giving to drink, or giving to drink before feeding, would be permissible were it not for the regard for beauty of composition. Then He conjoined the second with the fāʾ, because healing follows illness without any period of time empty of one of them. Then He conjoined the third with ثم, because the giving of life is after death by a period of time, and for this reason ثم, which is for delay, was brought in conjoining it. This is among the secrets that a writer ought to be acquainted with so that he may measure by them and conjoin each with what suits it and falls in the place of correctness.
4- Tafwīf (the multi-coloured):
We have not previously spoken in the preceding parts of our book about this art. It is the speaker's bringing various meanings of praise, description, amatory prelude and other arts, each art in a clause separated from its sister by rhymed prose (sajʿ) for the most part, with the clauses equal in resonance. It may be with long clauses, medium clauses and short clauses. An example composed of long clauses: «الذي خلقني فهو يهدين» to His words «وألحقني بالصالحين». In these verses are various arts, among them:
A- Appropriateness (al-munāsaba):
In his words «خلقني» and «يطعمني».
B- Al-tankīt (the pointed remark):
In his words «وإذا مرضت فهو يشفين». The point which obliged al-Khalīl [i.e. Abraham] to ascribe the act of illness to himself, apart from the other acts, is good manners with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, since he ascribed all the acts of good to Him and ascribed the act of evil to himself; and also to indicate that many illnesses occur through a person's neglect in his food and drink and so on.
C- Beauty of arrangement (ḥusn al-nasaq):
He put first the creation, for the creature's reckoning of the Creator, and the creature's acknowledgment of His favour, must come first, since it is the first favour, and in the creature's acknowledgment of the favour of bringing into existence from nothing is his acknowledgment of the Creator's power to bring into existence and originate, and of His wisdom. Then he followed with the favour of guidance, which is more deserving of precedence after the favour of existence than all other favours; then he put third feeding and giving to drink, which are the substance of life, and through them, from Allah, continued survival to the appointed term. Then he mentioned illness and ascribed it to himself, out of courtesy, as we said, with his Lord; then he followed the mention of illness with the mention of healing, ascribing it to his Lord; then he mentioned the causing of death, ascribing its act to his Lord, to complete the praise with absolute power over everything, of bringing into being and annihilating; then he followed the mention of death with the mention of giving life after death, and in it, along with the acknowledgment of this favour and the confession of power, is faith in the Resurrection. All these meanings are clauses whose wordings are conjoined, some to others, by particles suited to the meanings of the conjoined clauses, as has gone before.
D- Soundness of division (ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm):
These verses have comprehended the categories of worldly and otherworldly favours: creation, guidance, feeding, giving to drink, illness, healing, death, life, faith in the Resurrection, and the forgiveness of sin.

5- Transition (al-takhalluṣ):
This is a wonderful art, in which the author of the speech takes up one meaning, and while he is in it he takes up another meaning, making the first a cause for it, so that parts take hold of one another's necks, without cutting off his speech, but rather all his speech is as if poured out in one cast. Among the instances of takhalluṣ is this verse, which intoxicates minds and enchants intellects. Do you not see how well Abraham arranged his speech with the polytheists, when he first asked them what they worship, a question of confirmation, not of inquiry; then he cast blame upon their gods and nullified their affair, since they neither harm nor benefit, neither understand nor hear; and upon the imitation of their ancient forefathers, which he broke and took out of being even a doubt, let alone a proof. Then he wished to move from that to the mention of the God to whom alone worship is due and to whom alone return and turning are fitting; so he pictured the matter in himself rather than in them: «فإنهم عدو لي», in the sense: "I thought about my case and saw that my worship of them is worship of the enemy, who is Satan, so I avoided them and preferred the worship of Him in whose hand is all good." And he showed them by that that it was advice which he gave to himself, that they might look and say: "Abraham advised us only with what he advised himself", which is more likely to bring acceptance of his word and more urging to listen to him; had he said "they are an enemy to you", it would not have been of this standing. So at his depicting the matter in himself he transitioned to the mention of Allah the Exalted, attributing to Him those great attributes, magnifying His standing and enumerating His favours from the time He created and brought him forth until the time He takes him in death, together with what is hoped in the Hereafter of His mercy, so that it might be known from this that He who has these attributes is worthy of worship, and that submission to Him and humility before His greatness is obligatory on creation. Then he transitioned from that to what suits and fits it, and called upon Allah with the supplications of the sincere and implored Him with the imploring of the repentant, because the asker, when he precedes his request and entreaty with acknowledgment of the favour, is quicker in being answered and more successful in obtaining his petition. Then he inserted within his supplication the mention of the Resurrection and the Day of Resurrection and Allah's recompense of those who believed in Him and feared Him with Paradise, and of those who strayed from His worship with the Fire. So reflect upon these wondrous transitions deposited in the course of this speech.

6- Fronting (al-taqdīm):
In his words «رب هب لي حكما وألحقني بالصالحين» there is fronting: he first asked for the gift of judgement (ḥukm), then asked to be joined with the righteous. The secret in it is very subtle: the theoretical faculty takes precedence over the practical faculty, since one may know the truth though he does not act upon it, and the reverse is not possible, because knowledge is an attribute of the spirit and action an attribute of the body, and just as the spirit is nobler than the body, so knowledge is more excellent than reformation.
7- Mursal metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal):
In his words «واجعل لي لسان صدق» there is a majāz mursal, for the meaning of "tongue" here is praise, and the mention of the tongue is figurative because it is its cause, so the relation is causality, as has been said many times. It is also said that it is a figure from applying the part to the whole, because the call is with the tongue.

dervis-irab:10-17.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ نادى رَبُّكَ مُوسى: أَنِ ائْتِ الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): resumptive discourse, introduced to begin the narration of seven stories, which are in succession: the story of Mūsā, the story of Ibrāhīm, the story of Nūḥ, the story of Hūd, the story of Ṣāliḥ, the story of Lūṭ and the story of Shuʿayb. The adverbial is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being: "Remember, Muḥammad, to your people, perhaps they will take heed by it and take a lesson from the end to which the fate of those peoples came, who inclined to arrogance and obstinacy and resorted to contentiousness and fruitless sophistry." The clause «نادى» is in the position of the genitive through the annexation of the adverbial to it; «ربك» is the agent of «نادى» and «موسى» its direct object. As for «أن ائت», «أن» may be explicative or maṣdar, and it with what follows is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition. «ائت» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the weak letter, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; «القوم» is a direct object and «الظالمين» an adjective.
(قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَلا يَتَّقُونَ): «قوم فرعون» is a badal of «القوم الظالمين» or an ʿaṭf bayān, and perhaps the latter is preferable because the two expressions alternate on a single referent; and since «القوم الظالمين» suggested a shared reference, the ʿaṭf bayān came to remove it. The hamza is for rhetorical interrogation; «لا» is negative; «يتقون» is a nominative imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent; the clause is resumptive, and what is intended by it is wonder, that is, "marvel at their lack of piety". The sense of wonder must be implied, because the rhetorical question means negation, and «لا» is a negative, and negation entering upon negation is affirmation, so the meaning would come to be that they were pious, which is invalid. It is also possible that the clause be a ḥāl from the pronoun borne by the active participle, namely «الظالمون», that is, "they do wrong without being pious". Some parsers preferred that «ألا» be for urging (ʿarḍ), and others preferred that it be for alerting.
(قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي أَخافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ): «رب» is a vocative muḍāf from which the vocative particle has been omitted; «إني» is «إن» with its noun; the clause «أخاف» is its khabar; «أن» and what is within its scope is the object of «أخاف». The yāʾ of the speaker was omitted from «يكذبوني» out of regard for the verse-endings.
(وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسانِي فَأَرْسِلْ إِلى هارُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «يضيق» is conjoined to the khabar of «إن», that is, to «أخاف», so it is nominative like it; it is also permissible to conjoin it to «يكذبون», in which case it is accusative like it, and it has been read so. The difference between the two meanings is that the nominative gives three reasons or excuses, namely: fear of denial, tightness of chest, and the tongue not being freed; while the [second reading, which the source prints again as "nominative", evidently meaning the accusative,] gives that his fear is connected with these three. [Translator's note: the source says "وأما الرفع" a second time; the context requires "al-naṣb" (the accusative).] «صدري» is the agent; «ولا ينطلق لساني» is conjoined to what precedes, owing to an impediment in his tongue; «فأرسل»: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and «أرسل» is an imperative verb whose meaning is request; «إلى هارون» is attached to «أرسل». Mūsā did not mean to refuse to deliver the message or to hesitate in it, but he wished to show his incapacity to shoulder this weighty burden and to ask his Lord for help by supporting him with his brother so that they might support and assist one another in carrying out the command and conveying the message.
(وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنْبٌ فَأَخافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ): conjoined to what precedes; «لهم» is a fronted khabar, «علي» is a ḥāl, and «ذنب» is a postponed mubtadaʾ. It is his killing of the Copt who is said to have been Pharaoh's baker. The meaning is: they have against me the liability of a sin, which is retaliation for that slain man, so I fear that they will kill me for it; so the muḍāf was omitted, or the liability of the sin was called a "sin", as the recompense for an evil deed is called an "evil deed".
(قالَ: كَلَّا فَاذْهَبا بِآياتِنا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُسْتَمِعُونَ): «كلا» is a particle of rebuff standing in for a verb, namely "be deterred, Mūsā", and for that reason the fāʾ of His saying «فاذهبا» is used to conjoin to it. «اذهبا» is an imperative verb and the alif of the dual is the agent; «بآياتنا» is attached to «اذهبا»; the clause «إنا معكم مستمعون» is explanatory of the command; «إن» and its noun; «مستمعون» is its khabar; the adverbial is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl, or a second khabar, or to «مستمعون» itself, and the object of «مستمعون» is omitted, that is, "what goes on between you two and Pharaoh and his people". In this speech there is a trope that will be mentioned in the section on Rhetoric. [Translator's note: at this point the source text is damaged: the next sentence begins with the broken fragment «َأْتِيا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولا إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ», for the verse «فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ ...», the initial fāʾ having been lost, and the line break follows.] (فَأْتِيا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولا إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; «أتيا فرعون» is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; «فقولا» is conjoined; «إنا» is «إن» with its noun, that is, "each one of us", so that the khabar of «إن» may agree with its noun; «رسول» is its khabar and «رب العالمين» is a muḍāf ilayhi. Further discussion of this agreement will come in the section on Benefits.
(أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): it is more probable that «أن» here is maṣdar, because it is preceded by a clause containing the meaning of saying and its letters, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition. Al-Zamakhsharī insisted that it is explicative, in the sense of "that is" (ay), making it not preceded by His saying «فقولا» but by the meaning of sending contained in the word "messenger", as you say "I sent to you, that you do such-and-such," because sending contains the sense of saying, as in calling and writing and the like. The adverbial is attached to «أرسل», and «بني إسرائيل» is a direct object.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, the Exalted, «إنا معكم مستمعون» there is a trope whose meaning is: "We are with you, listening to what passes between you and him, and I am the helper of you both against him." Listening is thus the contextual indication (qarīna) of the figurative speech, because whoever hears the disputation of two adversaries is able to judge between them and to side with whichever he sees nearer to the truth and closer to what is correct. If an objector objects that Allah the Exalted is a listener and hearer in reality, and a trope may not be applied to Him, the Exalted, we say that istimāʿ (listening) requires attending with the ear, as seeing requires turning the two pupils of the eye, and all that is among the properties of created beings.

* Benefits:
It is possible that al-rasūl is in the sense of al-risāla (the message), so uniformity is permissible in it when it is used as a description, between the singular, the dual and the plural, as is done with a description by verbal nouns, such as ṣawm and zawr. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
ألكني إليها وخير الرسو ... ل أعلمهم بنواحي الخبر
(Gloss: "Carry my message to her; and the best messenger is the one most knowing of the regions of the news.")
He made it for the group because al-rasūl is originally a maṣdar, so it may be singular despite the plurality of its meaning; for that reason the plural pronoun in «أعلمهم» refers back to it. He likened the news to a place with directions, by way of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), and "regions" (nawāḥī) is the imaginative element (takhyīl); or he likened the concomitants of the news that are inquired about, as following upon it, to regions, by way of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya); he means that he is more knowing than others of that. And «ألكني» means "send me, accompanied with the message". Of the occurrence of al-rasūl in the sense of al-risāla is the saying of Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
حلفت برب الراقصات إلى منى ... خلال الملا يمددن كلّ جديل
لقد كذب الواشون ما فهت عندهم ... بسر ولا أرسلتهم برسول
فلا تعجلي يا عزّ أن تتفهمي ... بنصح أتى الواشون أم بحبول
(Gloss: "I swear by the Lord of the dancing she-camels going to Minā, amid the crowd, stretching out every halter: the slanderers lied; I never uttered a secret before them, nor did I send them with a message. So do not hasten, ʿAzza, to ask whether the slanderers came with sincere advice or with snares.")
Al-rāqiṣāt are the mounts proceeding to Minā in the pilgrimage; «khilāl al-malā» means among the people, in which case it is a lightened form of al-malaʾ, or in the desert, because al-malā is the desert and the wide expanse of land; al-jadīl is the halter on its neck; al-wāshī is the one who beautifies speech and colours it, mixes truth with falsehood and distorts words from their places. «ما» is negative, that is, "I did not utter a secret in their presence, nor did I send them to anyone with a rasūl", that is, a message; it is originally a maṣdar, though it may be applied to the one sent. The original is "yā ʿAzza", which was apocopated by dropping the tāʾ (tarkhīm). «أن تتفهمي» is "fī an tatafahhamī" or "for the sake of your inquiring"; «بنصح» means "was it with sincere advice that the slanderers came to you, or with ḥubūl?", which is the plural of ḥabl, with a kasra, meaning the great calamity, and there is no calamity more calamitous than lying.
